AI.method: 提出了一种名为潜在转移记忆（Latent Transition Memory, LTM）的新机制，它将交互历史压缩成连续观测之间的潜在转移。具体实现为LTM-π，它使用冻结的潜在动作编码器、轻量级适配器和因果KV缓存进行增量推理，无需记忆特定的语义注释或调用外部推理模型。
AI.result: 在RoboMME上达到58.54%的成功率，在LIBERO-Mem上达到80.5%的成功率，优于不使用外部推理模型或记忆特定注释的基线方法。消融实验证明了转移内容（超越时间线索）的贡献以及延迟记忆的效率。增加RoboMME演示次数可将成功率从57.67%提高到87.50%。在200个token的记忆预算下，成功率仍保持在84.00%。在真实机器人计数任务上，成功率从11.25%提高到82.50%。
AI.conclusion: 潜在转移记忆（LTM）在处理复杂的时序信息、在有限的上下文内操作以及在真实世界的机器人控制方面都展现了其有效性、可扩展性和效率。
AI.translation: 机器人操作通常需要能够记住那些不再可见的交互。我们引入了潜在转移记忆（LTM），它将历史记录存储为连续观测之间的紧凑潜在转移。我们的方法在$π_{0.5}$上实现为LTM-π，它使用冻结的潜在动作编码器、轻量级适配器和因果KV缓存进行增量推理，而无需记忆特定的语义注释或调用外部推理模型。使用DreamDojo转移，LTM-π在RoboMME上实现了58.54%的成功率，在LIBERO-Mem上实现了80.5%的成功率，在没有外部推理模型或记忆特定注释的基线中表现最佳。消融实验支持了超越时间线索的转移内容贡献以及延迟记忆的效率。将RoboMME演示次数增加十倍可将成功率从57.67%提高到87.50%，而“杯子交换”诊断突出了过程监督在时间组合中的作用。在200个token的记忆预算下，成功率保持在84.00%，而无压缩时为87.50%。最后，真实机器人计数成功率从11.25%提高到82.50%。这些结果共同证明了潜在转移记忆的有效性、可扩展性和效率，突显了其处理复杂时序信息、有界上下文操作和真实世界机器人控制的能力。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种名为潜在转移记忆（LTM）的新型记忆机制，用于解决机器人操作中需要记忆不可见交互历史的问题。LTM将历史信息压缩为连续观测间的潜在转移，并通过LTM-π的实现，利用冻结编码器、轻量级适配器和KV缓存，实现了高效的增量推理。实验结果表明，LTM在多个基准测试中表现出色，显著提高了机器人在复杂任务中的成功率，并且在有限记忆预算和真实机器人控制方面也显示出优越性。
AI.keywords: 潜在转移记忆, 机器人操作, 视觉-语言-动作模型, 上下文记忆, 时序信息
AI.comments: 该研究提出了一种创新的记忆机制LTM，解决了机器人操作中长期记忆和上下文理解的关键挑战。其将历史信息压缩为潜在转移的方法，在提高效率和性能方面取得了显著成果，尤其是在真实机器人控制任务中表现突出。然而，对于“冻结潜在动作编码器”和“因果KV缓存”的具体实现细节以及其泛化能力，仍需进一步的探讨。

title: CoDeFont: One-Shot Font Generation via Multi-Scale Factor-Specific Representation Learning
summary: One-shot Font Generation (OFG) aims to synthesize a target glyph by transferring the stylistic characteristics of a single reference glyph while preserving the structure of the target character. However, accurately capturing font style from a single reference image remains challenging due to the limited stylistic information available in a single glyph, and this challenge is further amplified for complex scripts. We propose CoDeFont, a script-agnostic OFG framework that addresses this challenge through multi-level style-content factorization and progressive style-content reconciliation. CoDeFont independently aggregates complementary style and structural information across multiple spatial levels to obtain factor-specific representations, while a contrastive objective explicitly encourages separation between style and content embeddings. During reconstruction, the disentangled representations are progressively injected through multi-level style conditioning, enabling stylistic information to be incorporated at different decoding resolutions while preserving the underlying glyph structure. We evaluate CoDeFont on structurally distinct Bengali and Latin scripts across seen and unseen font styles. Extensive quantitative and qualitative analyses demonstrate consistent improvements over existing state-of-the-art methods, highlighting the effectiveness of the proposed framework for OFG across diverse writing systems.

AI.title_translation: 通过多尺度因子特定表示学习实现的一次性字体生成
AI.tldr: CoDeFont是一个一次性字体生成框架，通过多尺度风格-内容分解和渐进式风格-内容协调来解决单字形风格信息不足的问题，并在孟加拉语和拉丁语脚本上取得了显著的改进。
AI.motivation: 从单个参考字形中准确捕捉字体风格具有挑战性，尤其是在复杂脚本中，因为单个字形提供的风格信息有限。
AI.method: CoDeFont通过多尺度风格-内容分解和渐进式风格-内容协调来独立聚合多个空间级别的互补风格和结构信息，以获得特定因子的表示。它还使用对比目标来分离风格和内容嵌入。在重建过程中，通过多尺度风格条件渐进式注入解耦的表示。
AI.result: 在孟加拉语和拉丁语脚本上进行了评估，CoDeFont在定量和定性分析中均显示出优于现有最先进方法的持续改进。
AI.conclusion: CoDeFont框架在应对一次性字体生成任务中的挑战方面非常有效，尤其是在跨不同书写系统的应用中。
AI.translation: 一次性字体生成（OFG）旨在通过转移单个参考字形的风格特征来合成目标字形，同时保留目标字符的结构。然而，由于单个字形中可用的风格信息有限，准确地从单个参考图像中捕捉字体风格仍然具有挑战性，而对于复杂脚本而言，这一挑战更加严峻。我们提出CoDeFont，一个与脚本无关的OFG框架，它通过多层次的风格-内容分解和渐进式的风格-内容协调来解决这一挑战。CoDeFont独立地聚合多个空间级别的互补风格和结构信息，以获得因子特定的表示，同时对比目标明确鼓励风格和内容嵌入之间的分离。在重建过程中，解耦的表示通过多层次的风格条件进行渐进式注入，使得风格信息能够在不同的解码分辨率下被整合，同时保留潜在的字形结构。我们在结构上不同的孟加拉语和拉丁语脚本上，在已见和未见的字体样式上评估了CoDeFont。广泛的定量和定性分析表明，与现有的最先进方法相比，CoDeFont持续改进，突显了所提出的框架在各种书写系统上进行OFG的有效性。
AI.summary: CoDeFont是一个新颖的、与脚本无关的一次性字体生成（OFG）框架，它通过一种新颖的多尺度风格-内容分解和渐进式风格-内容协调方法来解决从单个参考字形中提取风格信息的技术挑战。该方法独立地学习不同空间尺度的风格和内容表示，并使用对比学习来强制它们之间的解耦。通过在解码过程中多尺度地注入这些解耦的表示，CoDeFont能够有效地在保持目标字符结构的同时，合成具有所需风格的字形。在孟加拉语和拉丁语脚本上的广泛实验证明，CoDeFont在定量和定性指标上均优于现有技术，证明了其在处理不同书写系统和字体样式方面的有效性和鲁棒性。
AI.keywords: 一次性字体生成, 风格迁移, 多尺度表示学习, 对比学习, 脚本无关
AI.comments: 该研究提出了一种名为CoDeFont的创新性一次性字体生成框架，通过多尺度风格-内容分解和渐进式风格-内容协调来解决现有方法在提取有限风格信息方面的局限性。该方法在处理复杂脚本方面表现出显著的优势，并在孟加拉语和拉丁语脚本上取得了优于最先进水平的性能。其解耦表示和多尺度条件注入机制是该方法的关键创新点。然而，该研究可能未充分探讨其在更多样化或更复杂的书写系统上的泛化能力，以及计算效率方面的问题。

title: RenoLayout: Unified Floorplan Renovation and Furniture Layout for Constraint-Aware Residential Design
summary: Residential design aims to transform existing homes into functional living spaces while satisfying diverse design preferences and physical constraints. However, existing floorplan generation methods typically assume empty building boundaries as input, whereas renovation requires reasoning over existing floorplans. Furthermore, floorplan renovation and furniture layout are commonly addressed as separate tasks, overlooking their inherent spatial dependency. Consequently, practical residential design must preserve immutable structural components while transforming editable spatial elements. It must also optimize furniture placement under design objectives and physical constraints. To address these challenges, we formulate residential design as a design-point-guided conditional generation task and propose RenoLayout, a framework that translates a pre-design residential state together with a design-point set into an executable Geometry-as-Code program. To enable controllable supervision, we construct a Design Map comprising 123 fine-grained design points covering structural renovation and furniture layout. We further introduce Difference-Grounded Design-Point Annotation to derive design-point sets automatically from before--after design pairs with VLM-based consistency verification. RenoLayout is trained using a three-stage CPT--SFT--RL pipeline, progressively improving spatial reasoning, instruction following, and constraint compliance. We also introduce the RenoLayout Benchmark, a set of 200 real-world before--after renovation cases with complete furniture layouts. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first benchmark for unified residential design. These cases include design-critical structural and building-service constraints.

AI.title_translation: RenoLayout：面向约束感知住宅设计的统一楼层平面翻新和家具布局
AI.tldr: RenoLayout是一个新框架，它统一了住宅设计的楼层平面翻新和家具布局任务，能够处理现有建筑结构，并考虑设计点和物理约束。
AI.motivation: 现有楼层平面生成方法通常假设空建筑边界，无法处理现有楼层平面翻新；楼层平面翻新和家具布局被视为独立任务，忽略了它们之间的空间依赖性；实际住宅设计需要保留不可变结构组件，同时转换可编辑的空间元素，并根据设计目标和物理约束优化家具布局。
AI.method: 将住宅设计定义为由设计点引导的条件生成任务，提出RenoLayout框架，将预设计住宅状态和设计点集转化为可执行的“代码即几何”程序。通过包含123个细粒度设计点的设计图来实现可控监督，并引入基于差异的设计点标注方法，利用视觉语言模型（VLM）进行一致性验证，从前后设计对自动推导设计点集。采用三阶段CPT--SFT--RL流水线进行训练，以逐步提高空间推理、指令遵循和约束合规性。
AI.result: 提出了RenoLayout基准，包含200个真实的住宅翻新前后案例及完整的家具布局，这是首个统一住宅设计的基准。这些案例包含了设计关键的结构和建筑服务约束。
AI.conclusion: RenoLayout框架统一了住宅翻新和家具布局，通过设计点引导的条件生成解决了现有挑战，并提供了首个统一住宅设计的基准，能够处理结构和建筑服务约束。
AI.translation: 住宅设计旨在将现有房屋改造成功能性居住空间，同时满足多样化的设计偏好和物理约束。然而，现有的楼层平面生成方法通常假设输入为空的建筑边界，而翻新需要对现有楼层平面进行推理。此外，楼层平面翻新和家具布局通常被作为独立任务处理，忽略了它们固有的空间依赖性。因此，实际的住宅设计必须保留不可变的结构组件，同时转换可编辑的空间元素。它还必须在设计目标和物理约束下优化家具放置。为了应对这些挑战，我们将住宅设计表述为由设计点引导的条件生成任务，并提出RenoLayout框架，该框架将预设计住宅状态与设计点集转化为可执行的“代码即几何”程序。为了实现可控监督，我们构建了一个包含123个细粒度设计点的设计图，涵盖结构翻新和家具布局。我们还引入了基于差异的设计点标注，以从具有VLM一致性验证的前后设计对中自动推导出设计点集。RenoLayout采用三阶段CPT--SFT--RL流水线进行训练，逐步提高空间推理、指令遵循和约束合规性。我们还引入了RenoLayout基准，包含200个真实的、具有完整家具布局的住宅翻新前后案例。据我们所知，这是首个统一住宅设计的基准。这些案例包括设计关键的结构和建筑服务约束。
AI.summary: RenoLayout框架创新性地将住宅的楼层平面翻新和家具布局统一起来，解决了现有方法在处理现有结构和空间依赖性方面的不足。该框架通过设计点引导的条件生成，将住宅状态转化为可执行的代码，并利用细粒度的设计图和自动标注方法实现可控设计。通过多阶段训练和引入包含真实约束的基准，RenoLayout在空间推理、指令遵循和约束满足方面取得了显著进展。
AI.keywords: 住宅设计,楼层平面翻新,家具布局,约束感知,条件生成
AI.comments: 该研究提出了一种新颖的统一框架RenoLayout，解决了住宅设计中楼层平面翻新和家具布局的挑战。其主要创新点在于将这两个通常独立处理的任务结合起来，并引入了设计点引导的条件生成方法，能够处理复杂的空间依赖性和物理约束。通过构建详细的设计图和自动标注方法，实现了对设计的精细控制。此外，RenoLayout基准的提出为该领域的研究提供了宝贵的资源。然而，模型的泛化能力和在处理极其复杂或非标准建筑结构时的表现仍有待进一步验证。

title: SATOR: Backpropagation-Free 3D Test-Time Adaptation via Sample-Adaptive Token Routing
summary: Test-time adaptation (TTA) mitigates the performance degradation of source-pretrained models on unlabeled test data under distribution shifts. Recent backpropagation-free token-purging methods address 3D point cloud distribution shifts by filtering unreliable tokens. However, their reliance on predefined purge-size candidates requires multiple forward passes per sample and increases inference cost. We propose SATOR (Sample-Adaptive TOken Routing), a source-free and backpropagation-free 3D TTA framework that eliminates this search by deriving both the partitioning threshold and routing decision directly from each sample. SATOR computes token abnormality scores from complementary attention and geometric relation graphs. It then derives a sample-specific partition into retained and pruned tokens via Otsu-based separability, without evaluating candidate sizes. Keep-ratio-calibrated routing then selects the pruned prediction only when its entropy, penalized by the keep ratio, is lower than that of the original prediction. Experiments on ModelNet40-C, ScanObjectNN-C, and ShapeNet-C demonstrate that SATOR achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on three 3D corruption benchmarks.

AI.title_translation: SATOR：基于样本自适应Token路由的无反向传播3D测试时适应
AI.tldr: SATOR是一种无需反向传播的高效3D测试时适应方法，通过样本自适应的Token路由消除多轮前向搜索，显著降低了推理成本并提高了准确率。
AI.motivation: 现有的无需反向传播的3D Token修剪测试时适应方法依赖于预定义的修剪大小候选，这需要对每个样本进行多次前向传递，从而增加了推理成本。
AI.method: 提出SATOR框架，通过互补的注意力和几何关系图计算Token异常分数；利用Otsu方法直接推导分割阈值，无需评估候选大小；引入保持率校准路由机制来选择最优预测。
AI.result: 在ModelNet40-C、ScanObjectNN-C和ShapeNet-C三个3D损坏基准测试中，SATOR均实现了最先进的准确率。
AI.conclusion: SATOR通过样本自适应的Token路由和Otsu阈值分割，有效解决了现有3D TTA方法中高昂的推理成本问题，在多个3D损坏基准测试中取得了最先进的性能。
AI.translation: 测试时适应（TTA）减轻了源预训练模型在无标签测试数据上面临分布偏移时的性能退化。最近的无反向传播Token修剪方法通过过滤不可靠的Token来解决3D点云分布偏移问题。然而，它们对预定义修剪大小候选的依赖需要对每个样本进行多次前向传递，并增加了推理成本。我们提出了SATOR（样本自适应Token路由），这是一个无源且无反向传播的3D TTA框架，它通过直接从每个样本推导分区阈值和路由决策来消除这种搜索。SATOR从互补的注意力和几何关系图中计算Token异常分数。然后，它通过基于Otsu的可分性直接推导保留和修剪Token的样本特定分区，而无需评估候选大小。随后，保持率校准路由仅在修剪后的预测结果的熵（由保持率惩罚）低于原始预测结果时，才选择修剪后的预测结果。在ModelNet40-C、ScanObjectNN-C和ShapeNet-C上的实验表明，SATOR在三个3D损坏基准测试上取得了最先进的准确率。
AI.summary: 本文提出了SATOR，一个无需源数据和反向传播的3D测试时适应框架。它通过计算Token异常分数，并利用Otsu方法自适应地分割Token，结合保持率校准路由，消除了对候选大小的多轮搜索，从而在降低推理成本的同时实现了最先进的性能。
AI.keywords: 3D Test-Time Adaptation, Token Routing, Point Cloud, Otsu Thresholding, Backpropagation-Free
AI.comments: 该论文针对3D点云测试时适应（TTA）中现有方法需要多次前向传递来寻找最佳修剪大小的高推理成本问题，提出了一种无需反向传播且基于样本自适应Token路由的创新框架SATOR。通过结合注意力和几何关系图计算异常分数，并利用Otsu算法实现一步到位的自适应分割，显著提升了效率和准确率。

title: ESG-Kor: A Korean Dataset for ESG-related Information Extraction and Practical Use Cases
summary: With the expansion of pre-trained language model usage in recent years, the importance of datasets for performing tasks in specialized domains has significantly increased. Therefore, we have built a Korean dataset called ESG-Kor to automatically extract Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) information, which has recently gained importance. ESG-Kor is a dataset consisting of a total of 118,946 sentences that extracted information on each ESG component from Korean companies' sustainability reports and manually labeled it according to objective rules provided by ESG evaluation agencies. To verify the effectiveness and applicability of the ESG-Kor dataset, classification performance was confirmed using several Korean pre-trained language models, and significant performance was obtained. Additionally, by extending the ESG classification model to documents of small and medium enterprises and extracting information based on ESG key issues and in-depth analysis, we demonstrated potential and practical use cases in the ESG field.

AI.title_translation: ESG-Kor：一个用于ESG相关信息提取与实际用例的韩语数据集
AI.tldr: 本文开发并验证了首个大规模韩语ESG数据集（ESG-Kor），证明了其在自动化ESG信息提取和实际业务场景中的强大应用潜力。
AI.motivation: 随着预训练语言模型在近年来的普及，特定专业领域数据集的重要性显著增加，而当前缺乏用于自动提取日益重要的环境、社会和公司治理（ESG）信息的韩语数据集。
AI.method: 收集韩国公司的可持续发展报告，提取包含ESG成分的118,946个句子，并根据ESG评估机构提供的客观规则进行人工标注；随后利用多个韩语预训练语言模型进行分类性能验证，并将其扩展至中小企业文档及ESG关键议题的深度分析。
AI.result: 通过多个韩语预训练语言模型验证了ESG-Kor数据集的分类性能，取得了显著的性能表现，并成功展示了其在中小企业文档和ESG关键议题深入分析中的实际应用潜力。
AI.conclusion: 本研究成功构建并验证了韩语ESG数据集ESG-Kor，不仅证明了其在ESG信息分类上的高性能，还展示了其在中小企业及深度ESG分析中的广阔实用前景。
AI.translation: 随着近年预训练语言模型使用的扩大，执行专业领域任务的数据集的重要性显著增加。因此，我们构建了一个名为ESG-Kor的韩语数据集，用于自动提取近期日益重要的环境、社会和公司治理（ESG）信息。ESG-Kor是一个由118,946个句子组成的数据集，这些句子从韩国公司的可持续发展报告中提取各ESG组成部分的信息，并根据ESG评估机构提供的客观规则进行人工标注。为了验证ESG-Kor数据集的有效性和适用性，使用几个韩语预训练语言模型确认了分类性能，并获得了显着的性能。此外，通过将ESG分类模型扩展到中小企业的文件，并基于ESG关键问题和深入分析提取信息，我们展示了ESG领域的潜力和实际用例。
AI.summary: 本文介绍了ESG-Kor，这是一个包含118,946个句子的韩语ESG数据集，旨在通过人工标注可持续发展报告来自动提取ESG信息。研究通过预训练语言模型验证了该数据集的高效分类性能，并展示了其在中小企业ESG评估和深入分析中的实际应用案例。
AI.keywords: ESG, 韩语数据集, 信息提取, 预训练语言模型, 可持续发展报告
AI.comments: 该论文填补了韩语ESG领域专用数据集的空白，通过对可持续发展报告进行高质量的人工标注，并结合预训练语言模型验证了其有效性，同时展示了中小企业ESG评估等实际应用场景，对该领域的自动化信息提取具有重要推动作用。

title: Same Target, Different Origins: Aligning Latent Rollout for Consistent PDE Emulation
summary: Neural PDE solvers commonly generate multi-step predictions through autoregressive rollout, recursively applying a learned evolution operator and feeding each prediction back as input for the next step. Approximation errors can therefore propagate through the rollout, causing predictions at a shared target time to depend on their temporal origins and rollout depths. For a well-posed deterministic PDE flow, however, states at different times along the same physical trajectory should, under exact evolution, reach the same target state. To this end, we propose Align Latent Rollout (ALR), a regularization approach that promotes consistency across rollout origins through the neural PDE solver's internal representations. A second-order Taylor analysis of latent discrepancy propagation motivates two objectives: zeroth-order latent state consistency, which aligns representations at a shared target time, and first-order latent dynamics consistency, which aligns local evolution responses to shared perturbations. ALR can be integrated into different neural PDE solvers by regularizing suitable internal representations, without modifying their backbone architectures. Experiments across multiple PDE benchmarks and neural-operator backbones show that ALR improves prediction accuracy while reducing shared-target discrepancies across rollout origins.

AI.title_translation: 相同目标，不同起源：对齐潜在展开以实现一致的偏微分方程模拟
AI.tldr: 神经网络求解器在进行多步预测时，由于误差累积会导致不同起始时间的状态在目标时间点产生差异。本文提出了一种名为“对齐潜在展开”（ALR）的正则化方法，通过对齐内部表示来解决这个问题，从而提高预测精度并减少目标差异。
AI.motivation: 现有的神经网络求解器在进行多步预测时，由于误差累积会导致不同起始时间的状态在目标时间点产生差异，这与确定性偏微分方程的物理规律不符。
AI.method: 提出了一种名为“对齐潜在展开”（ALR）的正则化方法，该方法通过对齐神经网络内部表示来解决多步预测中的误差累积问题。具体包括零阶潜在状态一致性和一阶潜在动态一致性两个目标，并基于二阶泰勒分析进行推导。ALR可以集成到不同的神经网络求解器中，而无需修改其骨干架构。
AI.result: ALR在多个偏微分方程基准和神经网络算子骨干上进行了实验，结果表明该方法提高了预测精度，并减小了不同展开起源在共享目标时间点上的差异。
AI.conclusion: ALR是一种有效的正则化方法，可以提高神经网络求解器在偏微分方程模拟中的预测精度和一致性，通过对齐内部表示解决了多步预测中的误差累积问题。
AI.translation: 神经网络求解器通常通过自回归展开来生成多步预测，递归地应用学习到的演化算子，并将每一步的预测作为下一步的输入。因此，近似误差会随着展开的进行而累积，导致在共享目标时间点的预测结果依赖于其时间起源和展开深度。然而，对于良定的确定性偏微分方程流，在精确演化下，同一物理轨迹上的不同时间状态应该达到相同的目标状态。为此，我们提出了一种名为“对齐潜在展开”（ALR）的正则化方法，通过神经网络PDE求解器内部的表示来促进不同展开起源之间的一致性。基于对潜在差异传播的二阶泰勒分析，我们提出了两个目标：零阶潜在状态一致性，用于对齐共享目标时间点上的表示；一阶潜在动态一致性，用于对齐对共享扰动的局部演化响应。ALR可以通过正则化合适的内部表示集成到不同的神经网络PDE求解器中，而无需修改其骨干架构。在多个PDE基准和神经网络算子骨干上的实验表明，ALR在提高预测精度的同时，减小了跨展开起源的共享目标差异。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种名为“对齐潜在展开”（ALR）的正则化方法，用于解决神经网络求解器在偏微分方程模拟中多步预测时产生的误差累积问题。该方法通过对齐神经网络内部表示，确保不同时间起源的预测在共享目标时间点上保持一致，从而提高了预测精度并减少了差异。
AI.keywords: 神经网络PDE求解, 自回归展开, 误差累积, 对齐潜在展开, 正则化
AI.comments: 该研究提出了一种新颖的正则化方法ALR，有效地解决了神经网络求解偏微分方程中多步预测的误差累积问题。通过对齐内部表示来保证预测的一致性，具有重要的理论和应用价值。该方法易于集成且不依赖于特定的网络架构，通用性强。

title: Geometric Hashing in MPC with Applications to Clustering and Stochastic Embeddings
summary: In this paper we study consistent hashing (a.k.a. sparse partitions) for doubling metrics in the Massively Parallel Computation (MPC) model. A $(Γ,Λ)$-hash with diameter bound $Δ$ partitions a metric space into clusters of diameter at most $Δ$ such that every ball of radius $Δ/Γ$ intersects at most $Λ$ clusters in expectation. Consistent hashing has emerged as a central tool in geometric MPC algorithms. However, so far it has been solely used in Euclidean spaces, where it can be pre-computed. On the other hand, in cases where the metric space is received as input and unknown in advance, no previous parallel construction was known. We present the first fully scalable MPC algorithm over machines with local space $n^σ$, that given an $n$-point metric space with doubling dimension $d\leq O(σ\log n)$, samples a randomized $(Γ,2^{O(d/Γ)})$-hash in $O(d/σ^3)$ rounds. There is a dichotomy: if the doubling dimension is $d=Ω(σ\cdot\log n)$, a polynomial number of rounds is required to compute such a hash. We conclude by showing that this MPC primitive yields $O(d/σ^3)$-round fully scalable MPC algorithms for a broad class of fundamental geometric problems in doubling metrics, including stochastic tree embeddings with $O(\log n)$ expected distortion, constant factor approximation for facility location, bicriteria $(O(ε^{-2}),1+ε)$-approximation for $k$-median and $k$-means.

AI.title_translation: MPC中的几何散列及其在聚类和随机嵌入中的应用
AI.tldr: 本文首次实现了在Massively Parallel Computation (MPC)模型下对加倍度量空间的几何散列的高效并行构造，并解决了聚类和随机嵌入等一系列基本几何问题。
AI.motivation: 以往的几何MPC算法中的一致性散列仅限于可在预计算中完成的欧几里得空间，当度量空间作为输入且预先未知时，尚无已知的并行构造方法，因此需要在更广泛的加倍度量空间中研究可扩展的MPC几何散列算法。
AI.method: 提出了一种在局部空间为 $n^\sigma$ 的机器上运行的、完全可扩展的MPC算法，能够在 $O(d/\sigma^3)$ 轮内对具有加倍维数 $d$ 的 $n$ 点度量空间采样随机化哈希。
AI.result: 实现了在 $O(d/\sigma^3)$ 轮内对加倍度量空间的随机化哈希采样，并进一步给出了包括随机树嵌入、设施选址问题、k-median和k-means聚类在内的多项高效MPC算法。
AI.conclusion: 论文成功设计了在MPC模型中针对加倍度量空间的几何散列算法，并证明了其在解决聚类和随机嵌入等基本几何问题上的高效性，同时指出了算法复杂度的下界和双分性。
AI.translation: 在本文中，我们研究了海量并行计算（MPC）模型中加倍度量空间的一致性散列（又称稀疏划分）。一个直径上界为 $\Delta$ 的 $(\Gamma,\Lambda)$-散列将度量空间划分为直径至多为 $\Delta$ 的簇，使得每个半径为 $\Delta/\Gamma$ 的球在期望上最多与 $\Lambda$ 个簇相交。一致性散列已成为几何MPC算法的核心工具。然而，迄今为止它仅被用于可以预计算的欧几里得空间。另一方面，在度量空间作为输入且事先未知的情况下，此前尚无已知的并行构造方法。我们提出了第一个在局部空间为 $n^\sigma$ 的机器上完全可扩展的MPC算法，该算法给定一个加倍维数 $d \leq O(\sigma \log n)$ 的 $n$ 点度量空间，能够在 $O(d/\sigma^3)$ 轮内采样一个随机化的 $(\Gamma, 2^{O(d/\Gamma)})$-散列。这里存在一个二分性：如果加倍维数 $d = \Omega(\sigma \cdot \log n)，则需要多项式级别的轮数来计算这样的散列。最后，我们表明该MPC原语为加倍度量空间中的广泛基本几何问题产生了 $O(d/\sigma^3)$ 轮完全可扩展的MPC算法，包括期望失真为 $O(\log n)$ 的随机树嵌入、设施选址的常数因子近似、以及针对 $k$-median 和 $k$-means 的双准则 $(O(\epsilon^{-2}), 1+\epsilon)$-近似。
AI.summary: 本文在MPC模型中研究了加倍度量空间的几何散列（一致性散列），提出了一种首个完全可扩展的MPC算法来采样随机化哈希，并将其成功应用到聚类和随机嵌入等基本几何问题中。
AI.keywords: Geometric Hashing, Massively Parallel Computation, Doubling Metrics, Clustering, Stochastic Embeddings
AI.comments: 该论文首次在MPC模型中研究了加倍度量空间的几何散列（一致性散列），打破了以往仅限于欧几里得空间的局限，并为解决一系列基本几何问题提供了高效的并行算法，具有重要的理论意义。

title: Agentic Dependency Transformations: Lessons from an Exploratory Case Study of Flask
summary: Modern software relies heavily on third-party libraries, requiring maintainers to balance the benefits of reuse against dependency-related maintenance and risk. We define dependency transformation as an emerging approach in which an AI coding agent alters how a repository handles external dependencies. Local reimplementation is one transformation strategy that recreates required functionality as local code; dependency transformation is broader and may include other strategies. In this emerging-results paper, we report an exploratory case study of Flask to explore dependency transformation strategies. We design experiments that show how available context shapes an agent's dependency discovery and iterative transformation of dependencies. The case yields five preliminary lessons. These lessons and the five-part research agenda position dependency transformation as an emerging research direction and motivate explicit transformation contracts, provenance constraints, preservation requirements, and independent validation criteria.

AI.title_translation: 智能体依赖转换：来自Flask探索性案例研究的启示
AI.tldr: 本文通过对Flask的案例研究，探讨了利用AI代理改变软件依赖处理方式的新策略与方法。
AI.motivation: 现代软件严重依赖第三方库，维护人员需要在代码复用的好处与依赖项带来的维护和风险之间进行平衡，因此需要探索利用AI编码代理改变代码库处理外部依赖方式的新方法。
AI.method: 设计实验并对Flask进行探索性案例研究，探讨可用上下文如何影响AI代理对依赖项的发现和迭代转换。
AI.result: 实验表明了可用上下文如何塑造AI代理的依赖项发现和迭代转换，并从案例中总结出五个初步教训和一个五部分的研究议程。
AI.conclusion: 该探索性案例研究确立了依赖项转换作为一项新兴研究方向，并提出了五点初步教训及未来的研究议程。
AI.translation: 现代软件极大地依赖于第三方库，这要求维护人员在代码复用的好处与依赖相关的维护和风险之间进行权衡。我们定义依赖项转换（dependency transformation）为一种新兴方法，即AI编码代理改变代码库处理外部依赖的方式。本地重新实现是一种将所需功能重新创建为本地代码的转换策略；依赖项转换则更为主流，可能包含其他策略。在这篇关于新兴成果的论文中，我们报告了对Flask的探索性案例研究，以探索依赖项转换策略。我们设计的实验表明了可用上下文如何塑造AI代理对依赖项的发现和迭代转换。该案例得出了五个初步教训。这些教训和五部分的研究议程将依赖项转换定位为一个新兴的研究方向，并促成了显式转换契约、来源约束、保留要求和独立验证标准。
AI.summary: 本文通过对Flask的探索性案例研究，探讨了AI编码代理如何通过“依赖项转换”策略改变代码库处理外部依赖的方式，总结了五个初步教训并提出了相关研究议程。
AI.keywords: AI coding agent, Dependency transformation, Software maintenance, Flask, Exploratory case study
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一种创新的视角，利用AI编码代理来处理软件依赖项，为软件工程维护和代码重用开辟了新的研究方向。

title: Evaluating and Improving Static Application Security Testing Tools for Rust
summary: Rust has become a popular systems programming language in recent years because of its strong guarantees on memory and concurrency safety. Many types of system software have been re-implemented in Rust. However, Rust programs can still suffer from common memory and concurrency vulnerabilities due to unsafe code and misunderstandings of its complex mechanisms. To mitigate such vulnerabilities, developers often rely on static application security testing (SAST) tools. However, the effectiveness of existing Rust SAST tools on real-world vulnerabilities remains underexplored. In this paper, we first conduct an empirical evaluation of mainstream Rust SAST tools using security vulnerabilities identified in real-world Rust applications. We systematically assess their effectiveness, uncover common weaknesses, and analyze the root causes behind them. Motivated by the study, we propose TRUST, a large language model (LLM)-assisted automated testing framework. TRUST automatically analyzes the official Rust reference to derive and implement semantics-preserving transformations. It leverages these transformations to generate mutant programs for evaluating Rust SAST tools and uncovering potential faults within them. Overall, TRUST has revealed 46 faults across six popular SAST tools, 17 of which have been confirmed. In addition, our study yields ten empirical findings and four practical lessons that provide actionable guidance for developing more effective, robust, and maintainable Rust SAST tools.

AI.title_translation: 评估和改进Rust的静态应用程序安全测试工具
AI.tldr: 该研究评估了现有的Rust静态应用程序安全测试（SAST）工具，发现它们在检测真实世界漏洞方面存在不足。为解决这些问题，研究提出了一个名为TRUST的框架，该框架利用大型语言模型（LLM）和语义保留转换来生成变异程序，以评估和改进SAST工具。TRUST发现了6个SAST工具中的46个漏洞，其中17个已得到确认，并提出了10项实证发现和4条实践经验。
AI.motivation: 现有的Rust静态应用程序安全测试（SAST）工具在检测真实世界漏洞方面的有效性仍有待探索。
AI.method: 对主流Rust SAST工具进行实证评估，并提出一个名为TRUST的大型语言模型（LLM）辅助的自动化测试框架，该框架利用语义保留转换生成变异程序来评估SAST工具。
AI.result: TRUST框架在6个流行的SAST工具中发现了46个漏洞，其中17个已得到确认。研究还提出了10项实证发现和4条实践经验。
AI.conclusion: 现有的Rust SAST工具的有效性有待提高。TRUST框架能够有效地评估SAST工具并发现其漏洞，为开发更有效的Rust SAST工具提供了指导。
AI.translation: 近年来，由于其在内存和并发安全方面的强大保证，Rust已成为一种流行的系统编程语言。许多类型的系统软件都已用Rust重新实现。然而，由于不安全的代码和对其复杂机制的误解，Rust程序仍然可能遭受常见的内存和并发漏洞。为了缓解此类漏洞，开发人员通常依赖静态应用程序安全测试（SAST）工具。然而，现有Rust SAST工具在真实世界漏洞方面的有效性仍有待探索。在本研究中，我们首先使用在真实Rust应用程序中发现的安全漏洞对主流Rust SAST工具进行实证评估。我们系统地评估了它们的有效性，揭示了共同的弱点，并分析了其根本原因。受该研究的启发，我们提出了TRUST，一个大型语言模型（LLM）辅助的自动化测试框架。TRUST自动分析官方Rust参考以推导并实现语义保留转换。它利用这些转换生成变异程序，以评估Rust SAST工具并揭示其中潜在的故障。总的来说，TRUST在六个流行的SAST工具中揭示了46个故障，其中17个已得到确认。此外，我们的研究产生了十项实证发现和四条实践经验，为开发更有效、更健壮、更易于维护的Rust SAST工具提供了可行的指导。
AI.summary: 本研究旨在评估和改进用于Rust程序的静态应用程序安全测试（SAST）工具。研究人员首先对现有Rust SAST工具进行了实证评估，发现了它们的不足之处。在此基础上，他们提出了一个名为TRUST的新框架，该框架利用大型语言模型（LLM）和自动生成的变异程序来测试和评估SAST工具的有效性。该框架成功地发现了多个SAST工具中的漏洞，并为未来开发更有效的工具提供了宝贵的见解和指导。
AI.keywords: Rust, 静态应用程序安全测试, SAST工具, LLM, TRUST框架
AI.comments: 这项研究解决了Rust生态系统中一个重要的问题，即现有SAST工具在检测真实世界漏洞方面的有效性。通过实证评估和提出名为TRUST的新框架，该研究不仅揭示了当前工具的局限性，还提供了一种创新的方法来改进这些工具。LLM的应用和语义保留转换的利用是该研究的亮点，为SAST领域的研究开辟了新的方向。然而，所发现漏洞的确认率（17/46）表明，仍有进一步研究的空间来提高变异程序的准确性和SAST工具的检测能力。

title: From Optical Flow to Safety: Visual Safety Certification via Scale-Free Relative Motion
summary: Safe autonomous navigation using monocular vision remains challenging because explicit obstacle states are not directly observable. This letter introduces a visual safety-certification paradigm that uses scale-free, depth-normalized relative motion encoded by monocular optical flow as the representation for collision-risk certification, without reconstructing obstacle position, velocity, geometry, or a metric world model. Unlike conventional optical-flow-based navigation approaches that rely on image motion to shape avoidance behavior, the proposed framework directly encodes collision-cone geometry and safety constraints in this relative-motion representation. An online Concurrent Learning observer estimates the normalized relative velocity and provides a computable estimation-error bound. This uncertainty is propagated into the collision cone through angular inflation and a monocular robot-footprint margin, yielding a Robust Vision-Based Collision Cone Control Barrier Function (RV-C$^3$BF). An optimal-decay CBF quadratic program minimally modifies the nominal control input to enforce the resulting robust safety constraint under the stated assumptions. Extensive simulation and real-world experiments on a TurtleBot3 in cluttered environments with static and dynamic obstacles demonstrate collision avoidance using only monocular vision and onboard proprioception, with the estimation-error bound containing the measured error in $98.3\%$ of simulation samples and the robot achieving collision-free navigation in $93$ of $100$ real-world trials.

title: Memorilla: Latent Semantic Memory for LLMs
summary: Memory enables large language models (LLMs) to use information beyond their parameters, such as past user conversations, long documents, or an agent's earlier actions. For a frozen LLM, access to this accumulated knowledge is limited to what a memory system places in its context window. However, gathering and combining relevant information needed for each query while keeping the model's context short remains challenging for existing systems. Here we introduce Memorilla, a memory system that gathers information from an entire document collection into a fixed number of query-dependent 'memory tokens' for a frozen LLM. Memorilla encodes documents (such as user chats, book chapters) once into reusable embeddings, then learns to retrieve and place query-specific information in the LLM's input embedding space. Using only 16 memory tokens, Memorilla achieves the best performance against baselines including Mem0 and MemoRAG on five of eight benchmarks spanning personalization, long-document and knowledge-intensive question answering. Notably, on FactKG, it reaches 84.33% accuracy versus 80.43% with full-context inference, while using 108x fewer tokens to represent the source documents. Furthermore, Memorilla can facilitate continual learning in agentic systems where the document count (the agent's past turns) increases throughout the trajectory. In a TextWorld environment, we show that Memorilla reduces the agent's tendency to wander between rooms it has already explored, and improves its average success rate from 18.6% with full-history in-context learning to 24.2%. Overall, Memorilla aids frozen LLMs in accumulating and using knowledge effectively across long-context interactions and takes a step towards building continually learning AI systems.

AI.title_translation: Memorilla：大语言模型的潜在语义记忆
AI.tldr: Memorilla通过仅使用16个“记忆tokens”将整个文档集动态压缩并注入冻结的LLM中，大幅减少了Token消耗，同时在长文本问答和智能体任务中超越了传统基线。
AI.motivation: 现有的记忆系统在将积累的知识放入模型上下文窗口时，难以在整合相关信息与保持模型上下文精简之间取得平衡。
AI.method: 将文档集合（如用户聊天记录、书籍章节）一次性编码为可重用的嵌入，随后学习检索并根据具体查询将相关信息以固定数量（16个）的“记忆tokens”形式放置在冻结的LLM的输入嵌入空间中。
AI.result: 在八个基准测试中的五个上超越了Mem0和MemoRAG等基线，在FactKG上达到84.33%的准确率（全上下文推理为80.43%），同时Token使用量减少了108倍；在TextWorld中将智能体平均成功率从18.6%提升至24.2%。
AI.conclusion: Memorilla通过潜在语义记忆有效扩展了大语言模型的知识利用能力，在保持极低上下文开销的同时，超越了传统的全上下文推理和现有记忆基线。
AI.translation: 记忆使大型语言模型（LLM）能够使用其参数之外的信息，例如过去的对话、长文档或智能体先前的动作。对于冻结的LLM而言，对其积累知识的访问受限于记忆系统放入其上下文窗口的内容。然而，在保持模型上下文简短的同时，为每个查询收集和组合相关信息对现有系统来说仍然具有挑战性。在此，我们介绍了Memorilla，一个为冻结的LLM将整个文档集的信息收集到固定数量的依赖于查询的“记忆tokens”中的记忆系统。Memorilla将文档（如用户聊天记录、书本章节）一次性编码为可重用的嵌入，然后学习检索并将查询特定信息放置在LLM的输入嵌入空间中。仅使用16个记忆tokens，Memorilla在涵盖个性化、长文档和知识密集型问答的八个基准测试中的五个上取得了优于包括Mem0和MemoRAG在内的基线的性能。值得注意的是，在FactKG上，它达到了84.33%的准确率，而全上下文推理为80.43%，同时表示源文档所需的token减少了108倍。此外，Memorilla还可以促进智能体系统中的持续学习，其中文档数量（智能体过去的轮次）在整个轨迹中不断增加。在一个TextWorld环境中，我们展示了Memorilla减少了智能体在其已探索房间之间徘徊的倾向，并将平均成功率从全历史上下文学习的18.6%提高到24.2%。总的来说，Memorilla帮助冻结的LLM在长上下文交互中有效地积累和使用知识，并向构建持续学习的AI系统迈出了一步。
AI.summary: 本文提出了Memorilla，一种针对冻结大语言模型的潜在语义记忆系统。它将整个文档集编码为固定数量的查询相关记忆token，从而在大幅减少Token消耗的同时，在长文本问答、个性化以及智能体连续学习任务中取得了优于现有基线的性能。
AI.keywords: 大型语言模型, 记忆系统, 潜在语义记忆, 连续学习, 问答系统
AI.comments: Memorilla引入了一种新颖的潜在语义记忆机制，通过将全文档集合编码为固定数量的记忆tokens，成功解决了大语言模型在长上下文问答和智能体连续学习中面临的上下文效率和信息检索难题，具有极高的实用价值和创新性。

title: Does Compression Imply Generalization? A Minimum Description Length Perspective
summary: A central question in modern learning theory is what notion of compression, if any, explains why over-parameterized neural networks generalize. Existing answers measure complexity at different levels, ranging from weights to representations; however, estimating the associated quantities either requires held-out data in principle or relies on the challenging (ultra) high-dimensional mutual information estimation. To overcome these challenges, we approach the question through the minimum description length (MDL) principle, and specifically, we propose the prequential regret as a complementary signal that is computable from the training trajectory alone. We establish that, in the (nearly) interpolating regime, the expected prequential regret upper-bounds the description length of the trained parameter under the algorithm-induced distribution, and that this description length translates into a high-probability generalization bound in the PAC-MDL setting. Along the way, we show that the encoder-complexity correction recently added to the algorithm-level information bottleneck (IB) is upper-bounded by an MDL parameter description length, \new{bringing together} the two views of compression from MDL and IB. Empirically, the prequential regret tracks the generalization error on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, with Pearson correlations exceeding 0.9.

AI.title_translation: 压缩意味着泛化吗？最小描述长度的视角
AI.tldr: 本文提出利用最小描述长度（MDL）原理中的预序后悔来解释过参数化神经网络的泛化，该方法仅需训练轨迹即可计算，且与泛化误差高度相关。
AI.motivation: 现代学习理论中关于压缩如何解释过参数化神经网络泛化的现有方法，在估计复杂度时需要保留数据或依赖困难的高维互信息估计，因此需要一种无需这些挑战的新方法。
AI.method: 提出使用最小描述长度（MDL）原理中的预序后悔作为仅需训练轨迹即可计算的互补信号，建立预序后悔对参数描述长度的上界，并推导出PAC-MDL设置下的高概率泛化界。
AI.result: 理论上证明了期望预序后悔可上界估计训练参数的描述长度并转化为泛化界，且在算法级信息瓶颈中连接了编码器复杂度修正与MDL参数描述长度；实验表明预序后悔与CIFAR-10和CIFAR-100上的泛化误差高度相关（Pearson相关系数超过0.9）。
AI.conclusion: 基于MDL原理的预序后悔可以作为衡量过参数化神经网络泛化能力的可计算且有效的信号，并且统一了MDL与信息瓶颈（IB）理论中对压缩的视角。
AI.translation: 现代学习理论中的一个核心问题是，什么样的压缩概念（如果有的话）解释了为什么过参数化神经网络能够泛化。现有的答案在不同的水平上衡量复杂度，从权重到表示；然而，估计相关量在原则上要么需要保留数据，要么依赖于具有挑战性的（超）高维互信息估计。为了克服这些挑战，我们通过最小描述长度（MDL）原理来探讨这个问题，具体而言，我们提出了预序后悔作为一种补充信号，它可以仅从训练轨迹中计算出来。我们确立了在（近乎）内插机制下，期望预序后悔上限界定了算法诱导分布下训练参数的描述长度，并且这个描述长度在PAC-MDL设置下转化为高概率泛化界。在此过程中，我们表明最近添加到算法级信息瓶颈（IB）中的编码器复杂度修正由MDL参数描述长度上限约束，将MDL和IB的两种压缩观点结合在了一起。在经验上，预序后悔追踪了CIFAR-10和CIFAR-100上的泛化误差，Pearson相关系数超过了0.9。
AI.summary: 本文从最小描述长度（MDL）的角度研究了压缩与泛化之间的关系，提出了一种仅需训练轨迹即可计算的预序后悔信号，用于解决传统方法在估计过参数化神经网络复杂度时的困难。理论和实验表明，该信号能有效上界估计描述长度、给出泛化界，并与实际泛化误差高度相关。
AI.keywords: 最小描述长度, 泛化能力, 预序后悔, 信息瓶颈, 过参数化神经网络
AI.comments: 该论文从最小描述长度（MDL）视角切入，利用训练轨迹即可计算的预序后悔（prequential regret）来解释过参数化神经网络的泛化能力，成功连接了压缩与泛化，并且在CIFAR数据集上取得了极高的相关性，具有很高的创新性和实用价值。

title: DPA-MoE: A Runtime Precision Control Framework for MoE Inference
comments: 18 pages, 7 figures; Accepted to Findings of EMNLP 2026
summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models reduce computation by routing each token to a small set of experts, but each selected expert is still used at a fixed precision. We present DPA-MoE, a runtime precision control framework that makes routed experts any-precision. DPA-MoE encodes expert feed-forward weights as prefix-decodable chunks using SharedScale AnyBCQ, profiles per-expert reconstruction residuals offline, and allocates chunks at inference time using live router gate scores. This post-routing allocation lets a single encoded MoE checkpoint operate at multiple effective weight budgets without retraining or re-encoding. Experiments on Qwen3-30B-A3B and DeepSeekMoE-16B show that DPA-MoE improves KL divergence and downstream accuracy over uniform chunk allocation at matched budgets, with modest steady-state throughput overhead in our prototype.
comment: 18 pages, 7 figures; Accepted to Findings of EMNLP 2026

title: Model Checking HyperRecHML is Decidable
summary:
Temporal hyperlogics combine explicit quantification over traces with temporal requirements evaluated over the quantified traces. HyperRecHML is a temporal hyperlogic which allows for arbitrary mixing of trace quantification and the use of fixed points for expressing temporal requirements, which makes it very expressive in comparison to other first-order hyperlogics. HyperRecHML has already been successfully applied in runtime verification, but the decidability of its model checking problem remains open.
  We answer this question positively by providing two main contributions. Firstly, a normalization procedure that allows to reduce arbitrary HyperRecHML formulas to a normal form with restricted nesting of trace quantification and fixed points. Secondly, we provide an automata-based model checking algorithm for formulas of this normal form. The complexity of our algorithm is comparable to similar ones for other hyperlogics, despite the extra expressive power.

title: Perception or Reasoning? Diagnosing and Tackling Reinforcement Learning Bottlenecks in VLMs
summary: Reinforcement learning has brought strong gains to language model reasoning, but its improvements on visual tasks remain less consistent. One difficulty is that visual task failures can arise from different sources: the same benchmark may be limited by perception for one model and by reasoning for another. We introduce Perception and Reasoning Attribution (PARA), which measures the remaining perceptual and reasoning headroom of each model--benchmark pair by comparing how many current errors are recovered with more accurate visual information versus a stronger reasoner. Across 4 vision-language models and 17 multimodal benchmarks, PARA broadly agrees with the expected characteristics of existing benchmarks while revealing substantial model-specific variation. More importantly, it shows that RL gains become smaller as perceptual headroom increases, but larger when reasoning explains more of the recoverable errors, suggesting that current RL exploits reasoning headroom more effectively than perceptual headroom. Motivated by this gap, we analyze how existing RL objectives affect visual perception and find that reward- and token-level signals influence visual attention only indirectly. We therefore propose GRAD, a group-relative attention distillation objective that uses the best rollout in each group to directly guide the visual attention of weaker rollouts. GRAD consistently improves performance across two model scales and seven benchmarks, and further complements existing RL methods.

title: RDL-Bench: A Benchmark for Task-Aware Question Answering over Relational Databases
comments: This paper has been accepted by ICDE 2027
summary: Relational databases (RDBs) remain the primary infrastructure for storing and managing structured data across enterprise and scientific domains. Natural-language (NL) interfaces to RDBs aim to let users ask questions without writing SQL, but real user needs go beyond SQL-style lookup: some questions require reasoning over the observable database state, while others require predictive inference from historical relational records under temporal constraints. Existing benchmarks address these goals in isolation. To address this gap, we introduce RDL-Bench, a benchmark for task-aware question answering (QA) over real RDBs. RDL-Bench organizes diverse user questions into reasoning-oriented questions, whose answers are determined by the current database state, and prediction-oriented questions, whose answers depend on future outcomes under temporal constraints. Each instance contains an NL question, task metadata, schema information, temporal context, either executable evidence or target-construction logic, and denotation-level ground truth. RDL-Bench supports two evaluation settings: native solvers under their intended capabilities, and task-aware modular systems where a router dispatches each question to an appropriate execution module.
comment: This paper has been accepted by ICDE 2027

title: Calibration Language Shapes Block-Influence Pruning in Multilingual Language Models
summary: Block Influence (BI) ranks Transformer blocks for depth pruning from their input-output cosine change, but the ranking depends on the calibration distribution. We study whether English calibration transfers to Indian languages in Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, Llama-3.2-1B, and Gemma-2-2B. English, Hindi, Marathi, and Tamil use disjoint Wikipedia articles for calibration and evaluation; every selector receives the same 150-chunk budget, and Tamil is excluded from multilingual aggregation to test cross-script transfer. Across all three models, late-block BI is 20.7-55.5% higher for the three Indian languages than for English, and every predeclared late-minus-middle contrast has a 95% bootstrap interval above zero. This mismatch changes the low-BI blocks selected for removal despite high global rank correlations. Averaging BI over equal English, Hindi, and Marathi budgets mitigates the resulting perplexity damage for Qwen at six removed blocks and for Gemma at all tested depths, including held-out Tamil. The mitigation is not universal: on Llama, balancing improves Hindi and Marathi at two removed blocks but severely harms Tamil, while larger pruning budgets select the same blocks and collapse perplexity regardless of calibration. Rank-mean and minimax-rank aggregators do not dominate the raw mean. These results support a diagnostic claim rather than a universal pruning rule: English-only BI systematically misses late-layer activity for Indian-language text, but multilingual calibration must still be validated per architecture and pruning budget.

title: AdapTest: Supporting Designers in Authoring and Evaluating Environmentally Responsive User Interfaces for Extended Reality
summary: Extended Reality (XR) headsets increasingly host familiar 2D user interfaces as windows floating in physical environments. However, their usability depends on environmental conditions that designers cannot fully control. Current design workflows often separate how a variant is designed from how it actually looks in the target environment. We present AdapTest, an in-situ authoring and testing tool that lets designers select interface elements, define when and how they change, compare the resulting variations, and test their activation without coding. Based on prior research and a formative study with 12 interface designers, the system targets three key environmental variables: distance, lighting, and occlusion. We evaluated AdapTest against a desktop design and in-headset preview workflow in a within-subjects study with 12 designers. Compared with the baseline, designers accounted for a wider range of environmental factors, addressed more overlapping conditions, and repeatedly tested and revised their designs in place; there were no significant differences in workload or usability despite longer sessions. Our work contributes an integrated, designer-centered approach to adapting, comparing, and validating environmentally responsive XR user interfaces.

title: Top-Down Microarchitecture Analysis Without Causal Modelling Is Dangerous!
summary:
Top-Down Microarchitecture Analysis (TMA) is the standard for identifying CPU bottlenecks. However, TMA implicitly models performance via a single causal path: Workload(dataset, algorithm) => CPU(CPI) => System(Performance) (microarchitectural efficiency path). It overlooks two hidden causal paths: Workload(dataset, algorithm) => Instructions(Retired) => System(Performance) (algorithmic efficiency path) and Workload(dataset, algorithm) => Instructions(Retired) => CPU(CPI) => System(Performance) (microarchitecture-algorithm efficiency path). This causal blindness often misleads architects into futile hardware optimizations. To address this, we propose Causal Top-Down Microarchitecture Analysis (CTMA). Utilizing the object causal model, CTMA explicitly models these three causal paths among the workload, instructions, CPU, and system.
  We validate CTMA across Intel, AMD, and ARM platforms. Our experiments reveal counterintuitive insights: (1) CPI Profiling Blindness: Algorithmic instruction bloat can double elapsed time while the CPI profile remains frozen. (2) Over-Speculation Congestion: Throttling the Frontend paradoxically improves performance in pointer-chasing algorithms. (3) ILP Window Collapse: Extreme data topologies shift bottlenecks from Backend ROB capacity to Frontend fill-rate starvation. (4) Op-Cache SMT Overlap: Ultra-small footprints yield SMT speedups on Intel but cause severe thrashing on AMD. (5) "Ghost State" Artifact: Stale pipeline mitigations on Intel Xeon Gold 5120T artificially boost performance by 22.75% on SPEC CPU2017 and 42.2% on SPEC CPU2026. Based on this, we propose a dynamic speculation throttling mechanism.

title: Fast-VLA: You Only Think Once for Robot Manipulation
comments: 16 pages, 6 figures, 9 tables. Project page: https://garfield-kh.github.io/FastVLA
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies commonly place a multi-billion-parameter model inside the feedback loop, repeatedly recomputing task context whenever they predict a new action chunk. Yet task understanding changes far more slowly than the robot state. We introduce Fast-VLA, which invokes a frozen 4B VLM once per episode to contextualize the instruction and initial views as fixed, multi-layer key-value task memory. During execution, a lightweight online actor fuses learned time- and arm-indexed queries with current visual and proprioceptive feedback to form action queries. These queries retrieve task context from the fixed memory and predict action chunks without re-running the foundation model. Fast-VLA achieves 92.46% and 92.40% success on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean and Randomized, and 95.95% and 79.11% on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus evaluation. Against three continually conditioned baselines on the same hardware, it reduces RoboTwin amortized policy inference time by 10.9-17.1x and requires 1.22 GiB of post-prefill online resident memory. Task-memory swaps further show that the actor relies on episode-matched task memory. These results show that task context can be established once while closed-loop control remains responsive throughout execution. Project page: https://garfield-kh.github.io/FastVLA
comment: 16 pages, 6 figures, 9 tables. Project page: https://garfield-kh.github.io/FastVLA

title: PriorityFEC: Deadline-Aware Streaming FEC for KV-Cache Handoff in Edge Multi-Agent Systems
summary: Multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems are increasingly deployed at the edge to support complex tasks that require collaboration and information exchange among multiple agents. However, when task contexts are passed across agents, shared context that has already been processed by upstream agents often needs to be prefilled again, resulting in substantial redundant computation. Reusing an already prefilled key--value (KV) cache can avoid this recomputation, but requires the reusable KV state to be transferred across the network before the receiving agent can begin generation. Under strict time-to-first-token (TTFT) deadlines and unreliable edge links, delivering the complete KV cache may be infeasible, making it necessary to prioritize and protect the most valuable KV information within a limited transmission budget. This paper proposes PriorityFEC, a utility-aware KV-cache handoff scheme that jointly exploits model-side KV importance and transport-side reliability. PriorityFEC first constructs a utility-aware source stream by placing high-utility KV blocks at earlier transmission positions. It then protects the ordered stream using a feedback-adaptive Streaming Forward Erasure Correction (FEC) mechanism, which schedules repair packets according to receiver feedback before the TTFT deadline. We implement PriorityFEC on a distributed edge LLM serving prototype and evaluate it with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct across multiple datasets. Results show that PriorityFEC achieves superior task quality over the compared transport schemes, with its advantages becoming particularly pronounced under stringent deadline constraints. These results demonstrate the importance of jointly optimizing KV-cache utility and deadline-aware transport reliability when reusable LLM state must be handed off across unreliable edge networks.

title: NOCE-Net: Representation Learning for Battery Operational Context via Nested Sequence Modelling
summary: Learning effective representations from battery operational history is essential for predictive health management and control-oriented applications. Existing approaches rely on response-dependent engineered features or short early-life windows, limiting generalisability and precluding use in prospective settings where future responses are unavailable. We propose NOCE-Net, a deep nested sequence model that learns control-enabling representations directly from raw cyclic operational or telemetric data. Our data pipeline, re-BatteryData, standardises heterogeneous aging datasets into semantically equivalent Full Equivalent Cycles (FECs) defined by absolute charge throughput, enabling end-to-end learning across diverse operational regimes. NOCE-Net combines multi-patch transformer encoders for intra-cycle dynamics with a GRU backbone for inter-cycle state evolution, operating on approximately $700$ batteries across ten public datasets spanning over $300$ operational profiles. In zero-shot evaluation on unseen battery chemistries and usage patterns, NOCE-Net achieves $13.7\%$ MAPE in voltage response prediction, outperforming strong long-sequence baselines by over $43\%$ while using $40 \times$ fewer parameters. Shape and component diagnostics of the learned hidden states reveal that the GRU's principal direction of evolution achieves Spearman $|ρ| \geq 0.95$ with the capacity fade trajectory on average across all datasets with monotone degradation profiles, including zero-shot test batteries, providing evidence that the representations encode degradation dynamics transferable to downstream tasks beyond battery response modelling. Code is available at https://github.com/BeArnab96/NOCE-Net.

title: Learning to Reason with Selective Internal Feedback
summary: Reinforcement learning from internal feedback can improve language models without ground-truth answers or external verifiers. However, confidence and correctness can diverge during training, and continued optimization of average self-certainty can increase confidence while degrading reasoning accuracy. We introduce SIF, a reinforcement learning method that combines comparative reward construction with selective policy updates. SIF compares ranked token-level self-certainty profiles across multiple windows and peers, assigning positive rewards only when both levels of voting provide sufficient support. Sample and group level filtering determines which responses contribute to policy optimization. Experiments on three backbones across 12 mathematical and scientific reasoning benchmarks show that SIF's final checkpoints achieve higher average accuracy than the best-validation checkpoints of Intuitor and Vigor, with a gain of 4.71 percentage points over Intuitor on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B. Further analyses show better retention of accuracy during continued optimization, while test-time training experiments demonstrate sustained improvements with as few as four rollouts per prompt.

title: Self-Guided LLM Reasoning for Error Diagnosis in Vehicle Routing Problems
summary: Vehicle Routing Problems (VRPs) are fundamental to many real-world applications. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have spurred progress in solving these NP-hard problems. However, most existing approaches assume that input instances are error-free, neglecting the presence of faults commonly encountered in real-world data. In this work, we systematically investigate the capability of LLMs to detect (and correct) errors in VRP instances, and identify key limitations, particularly in handling complex instances or errors that substantially increase the LLM's reasoning burden. To overcome these challenges, we propose a self-guided reasoning framework in which LLMs autonomously generate code that provides structured insights to aid in error diagnosis. Experiments across diverse problem settings and LLMs demonstrate that our framework significantly improves error detection performance, achieving near-perfect accuracy.

title: Matoi: Selective Revalidation of Consequence Evidence for Agent Authorization
comments: 55 pages, 4 figures. Includes an 18-page technical manuscript and a 33-page detailed supplement as ancillary files. Research preprint; not peer reviewed
summary: Matoi separates reusable consequence evidence from current execution authority and durable occurrence history. Its finite query-aware contract covers branches, ordered collections and negative lookups. A consumer reuses only its own checked evidence whose observations remain valid; signed requests, live grants, quota and uncertain outcomes remain separate obligations. Conditional correctness arguments distinguish locally serialized claims from nontransactional remote effects. Two studies strengthen cost attribution and domain evaluation. A 1,440-cell matched-wire study repeats 144 authored inputs. With compact input bytes identical, reuse reduces complete lifecycle cost by 3.49 percent in JS and 1.79 percent in Python. Combined representation/reuse reductions against full proof are 10.87 and 16.53 percent; five of twelve family intervals for the matched comparison cross one in each language. A prospectively frozen AgentDojo Banking mapping covers 5/16 user plans and 7/9 attack plans. Both governed strategies preserve five exact benign transfers and refuse 35 reused attack-plan/policy crosses. Pre-satisfied utility predicates are reported separately from completed work. These are original scripted synthetic tools, not autonomous agents or a real bank. Earlier studies retain cheaper protected-cache alternatives, policy-compatible phishing, provider duplication and post-claim revocation. Separate JS/Python consumers establish finite-profile interoperability within the same project; durable recovery rechecks evidence and retains uncertain reservations. The results support a bounded, auditable reuse and execution contract, not a new general incremental algorithm, arbitrary-tool closure, atomic third-party commitment or production superiority.
comment: 55 pages, 4 figures. Includes an 18-page technical manuscript and a 33-page detailed supplement as ancillary files. Research preprint; not peer reviewed

title: Watts If? A Benchmark for Counterfactual Reasoning About the AI Data Center Buildout
summary: An AI data center is committed years before it draws a watt: a few discrete choices (grid or on-site gas, evaporative or dry cooling, which county to file in) fix its capital, water draw, and carbon path, and LLMs are now asked to help screen them with no test of whether they track what each commitment rules out. We introduce DCBench-440, with two arms reported separately: 200 generative questions over STRIPS worlds for five US deal archetypes, with search-verified gold answers and no tested shortcut above 12% on any question type, and 240 multiple-choice questions grounded in quoted site records, emission equations, and stated scenarios. Across open-weight deployments, accuracy spans 12.5-71.5% (generative) and 58.3-92.5% (multiple choice). One skill fails everywhere: asked to list every action available at a decision gate, no model exceeds 4.0% exact match. The strongest list 72-85% of the actions that would change the project's state but omit most permitted actions that change nothing; with those excused, the best exact match is still 24%. Code, data, and other materials are available upon request.

title: Modular Inverse Dynamics and Wrench Recovery for Closed-Chain Mechanisms Using Path Assembly
summary: Rigid closed chains can admit indeterminate internal reactions even when their motion is fully specified. This paper develops a modular inverse-dynamics workflow that combines path-based motion reconstruction with recovery of uniquely determined actuator and joint-wrench outputs. Analytical second-order differentiation of assembled transformation paths supplies passive velocities and accelerations on a regular closure branch. Spatial Newton--Euler balances are then assembled over the physical body-and-joint graph. Established nullspace and dual criteria identify and recover unique outputs, while balance, ideal-joint admissibility and affine-family diagnostics assess nonunique reference reactions. Evaluation against Simscape Multibody uses prescribed motion of a seven-degree-of-freedom heavy-duty hybrid serial--parallel manipulator under common rigid-body, ideal-joint assumptions. The results show close agreement with the reference for passive positions, actuator efforts and uniquely recoverable constraint-wrench components. Reaction diagnostics support compatibility with the admissible numerical load family.

title: Climate Physicalization: Bridging Tangible Interaction and Data Visualization for Environmental Communication
summary: Raising awareness of climate topics, such as urban heat mitigation, requires communicating complex data to a broad audience. Data physicalization has emerged as a novel method to connect audiences to such complex topics through tangible forms while also leveraging interactivity to foster deeper engagement. This paper introduces an situated geospatial thermal physicalization prototype, designed to enhance communication and education of environmental information through hands-on engagement. The physical model depicts a 3D model of an urban neighborhood, with radiation data represented as a layered contour structure. The model incorporates three interchangeable climate adaptation scenarios, alongside an externally mounted, electronically driven solar path representation featuring multiple discrete LEDs that can be switched on and off at will. To investigate how people engage with the model, we conducted a hands-on qualitative lab study with 16 participants, using think-aloud, observational, and questionnaire protocols. Overall, participants responded very favorably to the model, highlighting the novelty of the visualization approach and its capacity to improve the interpretability of the presented information.

title: Fault Detection and Bit-Error Rate Diagnostics in Optical Wireless Links Using Edge-AI
summary: Optical Wireless Communication (OWC) systems provide high-bandwidth, spatially secure, and RF-interference-free digital transmission. However, direct free-space optical links suffer from extreme sensitivity to line-of-sight disruptions, optical attenuation, high ambient light saturation, and transmitter-receiver misalignment. Traditional channel diagnostic frameworks rely on external computing nodes or cloud-based processing, which introduces severe diagnostic latency and reduces edge node autonomy. This paper presents an autonomous, self-diagnosing optical wireless receiver node that integrates physical-layer signal telemetry extraction with an on-device TinyML classification engine. Built around an ESP32-S3 microcontroller, the receiver recovers 1000 bit/s On-Off Keying (OOK) digital payloads using a 5-sample majority voting mechanism while concurrently extracting real-time channel features: Bit Error Rate (BER), received signal voltage (Vsignal), Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNRdB), and ambient light baseline (Lambient). Evaluated against a Random Forest baseline (77.22% accuracy) and a floating-point neural network (78.48% accuracy), a post-training INT8 quantized TensorFlow Lite Micro model occupying only 3.32 kB of SRAM runs directly on the receiver firmware. The quantized model achieves 74.68% overall accuracy across four distinct operational conditions: normal transmission, optical filter attenuation, ambient light interference, and severe obstruction/misalignment. On-device deployment tests confirm real-time, deterministic fault classification, establishing a practical approach for self-aware optical IoT nodes.

title: Beyond Invariance: Factor-wise Selective Treatment of Shifts for Multimodal Learning
summary: Distribution shifts pose a fundamental challenge to robust multimodal learning. Existing methods typically promote invariance by suppressing environment-dependent variations, implicitly applying a uniform treatment to shifted information. However, shifted information can have different predictive consequences: some contributes little to prediction, some remains reliably informative, and some exhibits environment-dependent predictive effects. This raises a fundamental question: which shifted information should be suppressed, preserved, or attenuated? To address this question, we propose FaShift, a factor-wise shift framework that diagnoses latent representation factors according to their distributional changes, intervention effects, and cross-environment stability. By factorizing multimodal representations and evaluating these complementary properties, FaShift distinguishes non-predictive factors, stably predictive factors, and predictively useful but unstable factors. It then selectively suppresses, preserves, or attenuates their contributions, rather than enforcing uniform invariance. Experiments on MOSI, MOSEI, and CH-SIMS show that FaShift achieves the best ID accuracy and F1 across all three datasets. Compared with the strongest competitors reporting OOD results, it improves OOD accuracy/F1 by 1.5/3.6 points on MOSI and 1.7/2.7 points on MOSEI, while achieving the best reported OOD accuracy and F1 on CH-SIMS.

title: Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense
summary: To improve task performance while encouraging desirable response properties, LLM post-training often combines a primary reward (e.g., correctness) with auxiliary rewards (e.g., brevity or efficiency). However, how these rewards are aggregated can critically affect training outcomes. We show that symmetric aggregation, which treats reward channels equally, can induce a failure where aggregate reward improves while primary-task performance degrades, even when individual rewards are meaningful. We investigate this aggregation-induced failure through a one-step multi-reward decision formulation, characterizing when it constitutes multi-reward hacking. We prove that, under symmetric aggregation, deterministic conditional-mean GRPO converges to auxiliary-favoring behavior when auxiliary rewards are more reliably obtained, regardless of initialization. We propose Trust-Anchored Gating (TAG), which first elects an anchor channel based on the policy drift induced by optimizing each channel alone, then gates auxiliary credit on anchor satisfaction. Unlike calibration-sensitive static reweighting, TAG structurally eliminates credit for auxiliary-only outcomes while preserving additional credit for joint success. In the same analytical setting, TAG provably reverses this selection, converging to the primary-favoring action from any initialization when the primary channel is anchored. Experiments across Qwen and Llama models on mathematics and program synthesis reveal substantial degradation under symmetric, constrained, and normalized aggregation, whereas TAG mitigates this failure. On Qwen3-4B with a brevity reward, TAG achieves 0.581 pass@4 versus 0.220 for additive aggregation, while shortening responses by 44% relative to correctness-only training.

title: MemCut: Every Secret Leaves a Trail in the Long-Term Memory of LLM Agents
summary: Long-term memory has become a crucial component of large language model (LLM) agents, with most research focusing on retrieving relevant information accurately and efficiently. However, a dependable memory system must also forget sensitive user data upon request. To evaluate this capability, we introduce MemCut, a systematic benchmark for user-requested forgetting. Its 456 hand-designed secrets in long-horizon conversations have fully annotated evidence trails to test recovery after deletion, including from messages that never state the secrets directly. We propose two recovery metrics. Native recovery measures reader success through the system's retrieval, whereas residual recovery measures the same reader's success when directly given surviving objects traced to annotated disclosures or evidence. We establish three reference deletion baselines to test how far existing retrievers and write models support forgetting across five memory designs and four LLMs. Disclosure removal reduces native recovery far more than residual recovery. LLM-guided deletion of ten additional turns from twenty retrieval candidates leaves 39-76% residual recovery. Subset sweeps (144 facts, three systems, two models) show that widening the pool at a fixed budget reduces residual recovery more than deleting all original candidates. These sweeps identify candidate coverage as a bottleneck in the reference baselines.

title: Identifying Effective Strategies in Prompt Evolution for Stress and Emotion Prediction
comments: 4 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to the 2027 IEEE International Conference on Healthcare Informatics (ICHI 2027)
summary: Early stress detection and risk prediction are crucial for timely mental health assessment and support. While large language models have recently shown promise for social media stress prediction, relying on accuracy can obscure false positives. Also, prompt revisions yield inconsistent gains across models and tasks, with unclear links to strategy combinations and instruction changes. By comparing six methods on social media stress and emotion data across two model sizes, we found that GEPA and its extension combining instructions from two prompts (GEPA+merge) improved prediction over initial prompts in several settings. We also identified five prompting strategies associated with development gains. These strategies included directing attention to emotional evidence, distinguishing current from past distress, illustrating indirect cues, requiring emotional context, and guiding label selection. Moreover, we documented four observations across tasks and evaluation settings. In a separate set of searches, binary stress prediction improved early, whereas multilabel emotion prediction initially declined and partly recovered. The other three concerned incorrect or conflicting instructions, gains on small comparison samples that did not hold on full development data, and changes in selected prompts' development and reported test rankings. These findings identify effective prompt evolution methods, strategy combinations associated with gains, and task and evaluation limits, providing guidance for applying prompt evolution methods to social media stress detection.
comment: 4 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to the 2027 IEEE International Conference on Healthcare Informatics (ICHI 2027)

title: CLAD: Keypoint Matching Using Global Line Correspondences
summary: Traditional keypoint descriptors, such as SIFT (Scale-Invariant Feature Transform) and ORB (Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF), are computed from local image patches. They may be unreliable in scenes with repetitive patterns or weak textures, where patches at different locations can look similar. We propose the Contextual Line-Assisted Descriptor (CLAD), a keypoint matching method that addresses this problem by using global geometric context from line correspondences. CLAD represents each keypoint with a vector whose elements indicate its proximity to matched lines. It can therefore use the keypoint's spatial relationships to the lines in the scene. We use HOME (Hough-space One-dimensional Matching of Extrema) to detect both clear and weak linear structures and to establish enough line-to-keypoint associations to represent this context. Evaluations on the TUM RGB-D SLAM dataset and outdoor video sequences show that CLAD provides geometrically consistent matches that complement those obtained with traditional local descriptors. In repetitive scenes, where local descriptors may not distinguish similar patches, CLAD uses global structure to improve matching reliability. The method is computationally lightweight and practical to implement.

title: Jev-LiteMAS: Separating Decisions from Generation in Multi-Agent Workflows
summary: Multi-agent LLM systems rely on generative models for expert execution, workflow planning, and artifact review. Yet many coordination operations require only bounded decisions, such as selecting the next expert or judging artifact quality. Profiling three representative MAS frameworks, we find that routing and review account for 31.7-43.5% of generative-LLM tokens. However, replacing these operations with low-cost decision models introduces two interface gaps: generative planners produce execution plans and handoff instructions (planning gap), while reviewers provide actionable feedback for repairing flawed artifacts (review gap), which bounded decisions alone cannot provide. We introduce Jev-LiteMAS, a multi-agent framework that bridges both gaps by combining a lightweight decision model (Jev) with generative execution and feedback. To address the planning gap, Jev selects experts dynamically from the task and prior expert outputs, using accumulated context to ground subsequent execution without a pre-generated trajectory. To address the review gap, Jev screens intermediate artifacts against task criteria: passing artifacts proceed directly, whereas flagged ones undergo LLM re-review for acceptance or corrective feedback. Across four benchmarks and two backbones, Jev-LiteMAS reduces generative-LLM tokens by 12.7-54.6% over LAS, maintaining accuracy within 1.34 percentage points and lowering latency in seven of eight settings. Grounding routing in substantive expert outputs prevents up to 18.0 points in accuracy loss.

title: JevAgentHarness: Benchmarking, Deploying and Training Decision Models That Share Control with LLMs
summary: Large language model (LLM) agents now fix software, operate computers and serve customers, but their harnesses, the programs that run them, call a large LLM at every step, which makes long tasks slow and costly. Most of these calls end in a multiple-choice decision, such as which tool to call next. Decision models such as Jev answer these questions directly, at a fraction of an LLM call's time and price. We ask how a harness can delegate these decisions to a decision model with little loss of success. To evaluate decision models in agentic tasks, we build AgentDecisionBench, which tests them from isolated questions up to control of a running agent, on public benchmarks and our DecisionGym environment. The decision model most accurate on isolated questions solved only 69.5% of agent tasks, and without a fitted confidence threshold, delegating tool choices lowered success by 19.0 points. Building on these findings, we then design JevAgentHarness, which fits this threshold for each choice on the agent's own trajectories and lets the LLM decide below it. Because existing decision models never see the states an agent reaches after its own mistakes, we train AgentDecision-4B, an open 4B model, on such states with Jev's answers as labels. On tasks unlike its training data, the agent solved 91.5% of them with AgentDecision-4B and 82.0% with Jev. On tasks like their training data, 4B models trained this way made agents 81.1-89.0% cheaper and up to 2.5 times faster, without losing 3 or more points of task success. The models, data, and harness will be released at https://github.com/JevAgentHarness/JevAgentHarness.

title: Learning to Forecast on Multiple Spatiotemporal Hierarchies
summary: Hierarchical forecasting exploits aggregation structures that expose multiple views of the same underlying spatiotemporal forecasting problem, while ensuring coherence among forecasts. Individual series provide fine-grained information, while progressively coarser aggregates reveal temporal and spatial patterns at different scales. In the associated deep learning architectures, the hierarchy determines which aggregate series are available and how they are processed together with individual series (e.g., through reconciliation or message-passing operators). Different hierarchies thus provide distinct learning signals and inductive biases for forecasting the same collection of time series. Nonetheless, existing architectures are typically trained on a single, often fixed, structure. In this work, we propose a graph deep learning framework that leverages variations across hierarchies as multi-task regularization. We show that jointly learning across these structures can reduce over-specialization to any single hierarchy and improve forecasting performance. Indeed, training across hierarchies provides an inductive bias toward representations that are useful across different structures, and as such, generalize better. Making forecasts coherent with the aggregation constraints for each sampled hierarchy is computationally expensive: to complement the framework, we propose a novel operator-based on a top-down approach-that produces coherent forecasts with linear time and space complexity w.r.t. the hierarchy size. Experiments show that our approach improves forecasting accuracy over training on a single structure and is competitive with current state-of-the-art methods.

title: Decoding Failure Biases IBLT Count Measurements: A Gaussian-Selection Law at the Peeling Threshold
summary:
In a self-sizing set-reconciliation protocol, a small first-round Invertible Bloom Lookup Table (IBLT) sketch attempts peeling decoding; after failure, the protocol estimates the difference count $d$ from the count energy and sizes the second round from a lower quantile of the measurement. This quantile must be computed conditionally on failure: the measurement and peeling success are determined by the same random mapping, so conditioning can shift the measurement law.
  In the ideal peeling model, inside the critical window where failure has nondegenerate probability, the standardized energy and a statistic of the unsigned mapping that governs the peeling outcome (the precritical score) have a joint Gaussian limit with correlation $η_kρ^2$, $ρ$ being the sign imbalance and $η_k$ a closed-form constant. The measurement conditional on failure is thus a bivariate normal truncated to a half-plane, which we call the Gaussian-selection law. Since $η_k$ changes sign between $k=4$ and $k=5$, under one-sided imbalance the unconditional threshold undercovers exactly when $k\ge5$ and is conservative for $k=3,4$.
  The key tool is a quenched CLT for a signed quadratic form on a random overlap graph; under asymptotically balanced signs, conditioning on any unsigned mapping event that is permutation-invariant and has probability bounded away from zero leaves the standard normal limit unchanged. After failure the protocol observes the total sign; inverting the selection law yields an upper confidence bound for $d$, asymptotically conservative in the critical window and, when $d/\sqrt M\to\infty$, along the whole load axis. The experiments use analytic constants, none fitted; the unconditional threshold carries a selection error that does not vanish with scale, while the corrected selection-law threshold matches per-configuration empirical quantiles.

title: What Does History Add? Calendar Controls and Information-Timing Audits for University Trajectory Forecasting
comments: 12 pages, 3 figures, 6 tables. Methodological simulator evaluation with information-timing and calendar-control audits
summary: We audit the predictive value of historical summaries in a rule-based university trajectory simulator. Seventeen ridge specifications and persistence separate current plans, past-state and past-plan summaries, and calendar-only history-length indicators. Across training, validation and two family-held-out evaluations, we reconstruct 16,750 routes and 804,000 monthly records. On the original 40-family set, six-month history lowers six-step normalized RMSE from 0.159234 to 0.151522, but its difference from a length-only control is -0.000895 (descriptive paired 95% interval [-0.001957,0.000248]). Fixed weights on 30 families unused in identified prior tasks reproduce this pattern: 0.156480 to 0.150074 versus current-state prediction, but -0.000558 [-0.001783,0.000728] versus the length control. These uncertain comparisons do not generalize to all-history summaries, which improve on their own calendar control. Exploratory decomposition finds clearer preparation-index and funds benefits, whereas fatigue dominates the six-month model's loss and has an uncertain length-controlled benefit. Moreover, 28.20% of its six-step fatigue predictions violate the simulator's [5,90] support. We document family dependence, prior exposure, strict temporal indexing, matched recursive references and independent numerical replay. The task conditions on recorded future plans; it does not evaluate real-student forecasts, causal action effects, autonomous planning or language-model memory. This is an evaluation audit, not a new memory architecture.
comment: 12 pages, 3 figures, 6 tables. Methodological simulator evaluation with information-timing and calendar-control audits

title: The Role of Agentic Instruction Categories for Code Generation: A Study of Five Python Libraries
summary: Agentic coding systems increasingly rely on repository-level agent files, such as AGENTS.md, to communicate project knowledge and developer intent. However, it remains unclear which categories of agent instructions enable efficient agent-file generation and accurate code generation. We evaluate five instruction categories: Repository Overview, Function Description, Implementation Detail, Testing, and Reconstruction Steps, across all 31 non-empty combinations using two Large Language Models (LLMs), Gemma 4 and GPT-5.4, and five human-written Python libraries. Our study addresses two research questions, comprising five sub-questions, on agent file generation and code generation. Results show that the number of instructions alone does not determine token usage for agent-file generation, with substantial variation across models and libraries. Although most AI-generated libraries compiled successfully regardless of the instruction combination, functional correctness remained limited. No Gemma 4 variant passed all tests, whereas 12.99% of GPT-5.4 variants did. Function Description achieved Gemma 4's highest partial-pass rate, while Reconstruction Steps achieved GPT-5.4's highest full-pass rate. For structural similarity to human-written code, Reconstruction Steps was most frequently associated with libraries closest to the originals in Lines of File and total Cyclomatic Complexity, while Testing and Reconstruction Steps were jointly most frequent for File Count and Function Count.

title: Where, How, and When: Query-Guided Grounding for Video Understanding
summary: Understanding video content requires reasoning at multiple levels of granularity, from identifying objects to interpreting their interactions and localizing when specific actions occur. This thesis studies three query-guided grounding tasks that answer where key objects are (object-level grounding), how they interact (relationship-level grounding), and when specific moments occur (moment-level grounding). For object-level grounding, we present QDETRv, a query-guided extension of the Detection Transformer for one-shot localization of unseen objects in videos, which combines query-context fusion, a memory module for temporal consistency, and unsupervised pretraining on synthetic object trajectories. We further propose the Temporal Object-Aware Vision Transformer (TOViT) for few-shot video object detection, which builds on a language-aligned open-set vision encoder and propagates high-confidence object features across frames. For relationship-level grounding, we introduce few-shot referring relationships in videos: given a (subject, predicate, object) query and a few support videos sharing the predicate, the entities are localized by optimizing a T-partite random field using a meta-learned relation network with query-conditioned translational embeddings, Global Semantic Aggregation, Local Localization Aggregation, and belief-propagation-based message passing. For moment-level grounding, we propose the Moment Alignment Transformer (MATR) for video-to-video moment retrieval, which uses dual-stage Dynamic Time Warping for pre- and post-fusion alignment, learnable queries for boundary prediction, and self-supervised pretraining with temporal augmentations; MATR also extends to text-to-video moment retrieval with performance comparable to, or better than, the state of the art. These contributions advance query-guided video understanding across spatial, relational, and temporal grounding.

title: Do Agents Need a New Kind of Paper? SPRA: Structured Paper Representation for Agents
comments: 23 pages, including references and appendices; resource website: https://sciverse.opendatalab.com/
summary: Scientific agents must connect research problems, methods, and findings dispersed through narrative articles. We introduce SPRA (Structured Paper Representation for Agents), a paper-level representation of persistent research objects and typed relations. Its empirical-AI profile organizes Problems, Contributions, Components, ExperimentSetups, Measures, and Findings for querying, traversal, and reuse. Selected paper-level citation relations record dependencies, component use, and comparisons with prior work; source locations support verification. We instantiate SPRA across more than one million AI papers, with 19.95 million research units and 24.07 million internal relations. Evaluations access SPRA through Schema-RAG with task evidence fixed before inference. Across seven subfields, SPRA improves source-conditioned scientific QA by 0.381/5 over passage retrieval while remaining close to Full Compact (0.078/5 lower on average). In directed cross-paper reasoning, qualification improves by 0.184/5 over passage retrieval; Top-5 synthesis shows mixed quality effects. Across all paired RQ2 tasks, including Top-5, input+output tokens decrease by 28.5% relative to passage retrieval and 95.3% relative to Full Compact. In idea generation, a 0.067-point lower Overall score than Full Compact accompanies 93.7% fewer input+output tokens. Together, these results support SPRA as a usable representation of scientific content and a foundation for research workflows that connect, inspect, and reuse paper-level research objects. The SPRA resource is accessible through the SciVerse scholarly-data platform.
comment: 23 pages, including references and appendices; resource website: https://sciverse.opendatalab.com/

title: Multiscale Generalized Sparse Plane Wave Decomposition in the Spherical Harmonic Domain
comments: Accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Audio, Speech and Language Processing
summary: Sparse plane wave decomposition (SPWD) is a physics-driven model-based approach for analyzing sound fields that is suitable for real-time operation. SPWD is used in different contexts such as direction of arrival (DOA) estimation and sound field separation.
