Documents StudioCrit engineering and simulation evidence; related Critsly demo: arXiv:2607.09673. No human-participant learning outcomes are reported. v2 adds the AIEDx grant acknowledgement for Critsly's development

title: Structural Properties of DomiRank Centrality: Symmetry Axioms, an Entropy Bound, and Spectral Interpolation
summary: DomiRank is a node-importance algorithm for unweighted networks, defined by a dynamical model governed by a competition-strength parameter, a dominance threshold, and a decay rate. We establish three structural results. First, on symmetry. Automorphism-related vertices share the same DomiRank value, and a graph whose values are pairwise distinct must be asymmetric. The orbit count bounds the number of distinct values, and regular and vertex-transitive graphs admit closed forms. Second, on entropy. The maximum of the DomiRank entropy over connected graphs, log_2 N, is attained if and only if the graph is regular. The initial entropy derivative is the degree-log-degree edge covariance, making the decrease rigorous near vanishing competition for structurally disassortative graphs, and an assortative counterexample shows it does not extend to all graphs; a sufficient-condition theorem and a refined conjecture cover the rest. Third, on spectrum. The normalized distribution is sigma-invariant if and only if the degree vector is an adjacency-matrix eigenvector. The parameter sigma interpolates continuously between degree and smallest-eigenvector centrality within the resolvent (Bonacich-type) family, its sensitivity being a second-order suppression operator on the degree vector. Graph transformations are also characterized, including the m-product. Experiments on four real networks and synthetic families up to 10^4 vertices confirm the interpolation and exhibit monotone entropy decrease, continuous ranking interpolation, decaying positive fraction and ranking reversals; where the positive fraction has decayed far from one, the limit describes the solution vector rather than the induced ranking. DomiRank is thus a tunable complement to principal-eigenvector centrality. A companion study quantifies how much of its task-level edge over a degree baseline survives degree correction.

title: Testing and Verification of Quantum Compilers through Assurance Contracts and Evidence
summary: Quantum compiler assurance requires a semantic relation that matches the intended use and observations that can expose violations at the delivered interface. This critical integrative survey compares verified transformations, equivalence checking, differential and metamorphic testing, property-based testing, and evidence for assurance across revisions. A source catalogue and focused extraction matrix distinguish formal guarantees, reported empirical findings, analytical deductions, and proposed practice. A recorded coverage update and source-level selection decisions make the review auditable within its declared scope. Four documented failure cases connect conditional applicability, parameter association, termination, and phase conventions to method selection. A worked example involving layout metadata, parameter bindings, and ancillary qubits demonstrates why validating a circuit under a reconstructed interpretation can leave the delivered interface unchecked. An illustrative revision scenario then separates fault detection from change attribution. The resulting guidance specifies applicability, complementary observations, and treatment of inconclusive outcomes. Published bug counts, mutation results, and processing benchmarks support different claims and do not establish a common effectiveness ranking. The proposed regression architecture remains unevaluated as a complete system; its practical value requires controlled comparisons on independently adjudicated compiler-change events.

title: TeamLens in Critsly: A Consent-Based Team-Composition Interface and Synthetic Readiness Evaluation for Design Collaboration
comments: 16 pages, 8 figures, 6 tables. Technical software evaluation using synthetic fixtures; includes ancillary synthetic records and verification scripts. v2 adds the AIEDx grant acknowledgement for Critsly's development
summary: Discussing working preferences may support reflection within a design team, but a personality label should not become a performance prediction or a condition of participation. This technical report presents TeamLens, an optional Critsly interface for voluntarily sharing a self-reported MBTI type with a particular board. It separates account activation from disclosure, displays descriptive composition counts, and provides distinct controls for disabling visibility, withdrawing one report and deleting all of one's reports. The evaluation combines released-source inspection, independently specified synthetic aggregation cases, access and lifecycle checks, browser component tests, a local database microbenchmark and deployment records. All 65,536 binary eligibility subsets of sixteen fixed, distinct type reports matched an independent oracle; 128 seeded multiplicity fixtures also matched, after 4,259 synthetic share calls. The isolated HTTP suite passed 183 assertions. In 180 sequential in-memory SQLite read trials, median service-call time increased from 0.064 ms with no profile rows to 200.932 ms with 1,024 rows; instrumented SQL operations followed 11+3n. These findings concern exercised software behaviour and a bounded workload. They do not establish human usability, psychometric validity, learning gains, team-performance effects or production capacity. The contribution is an implemented disclosure-to-aggregation workflow and an auditable technical account of its correctness boundaries, privacy limitations and scaling cost. OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, evaluation and manuscript preparation; the paper discloses this use and its limits.
comment: 16 pages, 8 figures, 6 tables. Technical software evaluation using synthetic fixtures; includes ancillary synthetic records and verification scripts. v2 adds the AIEDx grant acknowledgement for Critsly's development

title: CompMat-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents for Computational Materials Science
summary: Evaluating AI agents on scientific research tasks is constrained by the time and resources required for the underlying experiments or calculations. In computational materials research, repeating the same expensive simulations across agents and trials can make evaluation impractical. We introduce CompMat-Bench, a benchmark of 94 tasks derived from recently published computational materials studies, each asking agents to complete a step toward achieving the study's scientific goal. We reproduce the research steps in advance and assess agents on preparing inputs and analyzing outputs for expensive simulations, so expensive simulations can be avoided during evaluation. The reproduced inputs and results serve as ground truth for grading agents with fixed rules, without an LLM judge. The benchmark supports four evaluation conditions: single tasks and workflows composed of related tasks, each with full or reduced methodological guidance. With full guidance on single tasks, agents based on three LLMs demonstrate the ability to complete individual materials research steps, with pass rates of 66.0-90.4% across 94 tasks. Both longer workflows and reduced guidance can limit agent performance, but in different ways for different agents: they lower the pass rates of the weaker agents, whereas the strongest agent falls only when a long workflow is combined with reduced guidance. Failure analysis attributes most failures to scientific errors rather than to errors in software usage. CompMat-Bench provides a basis for comparing agents on the steps of real materials research and for analyzing agent failure modes.

title: Autonomous OSS Threat Detection via Taxonomy-Aligned LLMs
summary: Open-source software (OSS) ecosystems face escalating supply chain threats, including typosquatting, dependency confusion, Trojan Source obfuscation, malicious build injection, and CI/CD pipeline poisoning. Sonatype documented over 1.2 million cumulative malicious packages across major registries, while signature-based and rule-based detection approaches lack the semantic understanding needed to generalize across evolving attacks. This paper proposes a taxonomy-aligned large language model framework for automated detection and multi-class classification of OSS supply chain threats. We introduce an AV-xxx taxonomy covering five semantically distinct attack categories and curate 999 verified real-world incidents from GitHub Security Advisories, CISA alerts, government security databases, and commercial threat intelligence reports, spanning 2018 to 2026 across eight package ecosystems. Using taxonomy-aligned prompting with GPT-4, the framework achieves 97% accuracy and 97% macro F1 across all five categories. Evaluation against eight methods five traditional machine learning baselines, one zero-shot open-source LLM, and two fine-tuned neural models reveals that fine-tuned Llama 3.1 8B (70.5%) and SecRoBERTa (77.5%) underperform a simple TF-IDF classifier (82.3%), while Mistral 7B without taxonomy alignment achieves 65.7%. These findings highlight taxonomy-aligned prompting over model scale, domain pretraining, or fine-tuning as the critical performance factor. Cross-ecosystem analysis shows varying classification difficulty, with npm achieving 65.5% baseline accuracy versus 100% in smaller ecosystems. GitHub Actions exhibits a substantial accuracy F1 divergence (82.4% accuracy, 0.367 macro F1), indicating systematic class imbalance and highlighting ecosystems where LLM-based contextual reasoning offers the greatest benefit. Our dataset, scripts, and code are publicly available in Github.

title: Global Coherence: When Every Agent Is Right and the Team Is Still Wrong - A Local-to-Global Semantic Foundation for Multi-Agent Collaboration
summary: AI agents can each make locally valid decisions yet jointly produce an invalid result. We call this the global coherence problem: a failure of shared state, not merely of intelligence. Our Observation-Aliasing Impossibility Theorem gives the exact boundary. A policy can guarantee a valid action exactly when all worlds producing the same observation share an admissible action. If k indistinguishable worlds require pairwise-disjoint actions, the best randomized worst-case success is 1/k; more reasoning, roles, messages, or samples cannot recover the missing distinction. A stronger model can reason better within its context, but it cannot see beyond it. The smallest sufficient context is NP-hard to find, yet counterexample-guided refinement finds a sufficient one and recertifies it as rules change. We give local-to-global runtime semantics X = (H, C, G, F; D): topology H records overlapping scopes; category C governs state-changing actions; groupoid G keeps reversible translations; sheaf F tests whether local views glue into one world; and history D keeps only what alters legal futures. Each preserves the needed information as state is split, translated, or changed. Models propose; the harness owns shared state and governs commit. Ten studies test the boundary. On a revision benchmark, a frontier model scores 40/40 when the deciding event is visible; hidden, every arm is consistent with chance (1/3); one restored fact returns 40/40. On TeamBench, ordinary teams exceed a shared budget in 5/5 runs, a visible live count leaves 4/5, and commit enforcement leaves 0/5. In tau2-bench Telecom, current-state checks score 0.07 after silent reverts; the harness scores 1.00. Refinement keeps a sufficient context through rule changes at 28% of the all-field cost. Solvers that already own the state tie it, as predicted. Local intelligence cannot substitute for missing global state.

title: UniWAM: Unified World-Action Model
summary: Vision-language-action models benefit from the understanding and reasoning capabilities of pretrained vision-language models, but action-only supervision provides limited grounding in world dynamics. Conversely, world-action models inherit spatiotemporal priors from video generation models, yet remain limited in semantic understanding and reasoning under distribution shifts. We introduce UniWAM, a unified architecture that integrates a physical reasoner, a world generator, and an action predictor to jointly learn semantic understanding of the physical world, visual generation, and action prediction. To ensure the quality of the training data, we developed a rigorous data cleaning and annotation pipeline for both human egocentric data and robot data. To adapt the vision-language component to embodied tasks while preserving its inherited language capabilities, we represent low-level actions in natural language and introduce a pre-training recipe that assigns complementary supervision from visual question answering (VQA) data, human egocentric data, and robot demonstrations to the appropriate model components. During post-training, future visual noise augmentation reduces reliance on precise future predictions, while history-conditioned flow matching uses encoded action history to initialize action generation. Together, these designs significantly reduce denoising steps while maintaining performance. UniWAM achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance across multiple evaluations, including in-distribution performance, robustness, generalization, instruction following, and long-horizon task execution. Furthermore, we uncover a log-linear scaling law of unified human-robot co-training, demonstrating the effectiveness of large-scale pre-training on a mixture of human and robot data.

title: Fixed-Capacity Causal Models with Parallel Recovery for GPU Lossless Compression
summary: GPU compression needs both dense complete frames and inexpensive checked recovery. We compare three causal representations under the same 512-row model budget, select before encoding one payload, and align entropy states with causal byte banks. Same-lane and residual banks decode concurrently; high-first banks decode in causal order. On ten reused structured/electrophysiology inputs, split-bank execution lowers aggregate median encode-plus-recovery time 13.10% for 0.18% more frame bytes. A separate twelve-configuration GPU comparison places it on the measured median frontier: 5.75% and 7.11% smaller frames than transformed nvCOMP Zstd at 35.14/19.03% lower paired cost for 64/8 KiB requests. A matched native-CPU model control isolates a 44.16% reduction in complete encoding cost; a CUDA-free CPU receiver restores the same frames. Three whole EEG recordings retain a separate Zstd-1--16 curve, while fixed ECG fixtures expose transformed-Zstd counterexamples. Model overhead, concentrated gains, technical ranges and adverse outcomes bound these operating points. ANS interleaving and transforms are established; reused inputs, unequal resources and fixed controls do not establish codec optima or population superiority.

title: A generative-informed neuro-symbolic framework for syntactic ambiguity resolution: Evidence from Arabic DPs
summary: Syntactic ambiguity poses a persistent challenge for Arabic NLP, particularly in morphologically rich nominal constructions where multiple structu6ral interpretations may be compatible with the same surface sequence. This study proposes a generatively informed neuro-symbolic framework for resolving structural ambiguity in Modern Standard Arabic (MSA) DPs. The framework integrates generative syntactic notions with AraBERT by representing ambiguity as a candidate-based decision task in which linguistically motivated alternatives are explicitly constructed and evaluated through candidate-conditioned input representations. Findings indicate that the model achieved 96.88% accuracy, 95.92% macro-F1, 96.83% weighted F1, and 93.94% binary F1 on the unseen evaluation set. Class-level analysis revealed asymmetric performance, with recall of 99.71% for High/VP Attachment (N1) and 89.26% for Low/NP/Embedded Attachment (N2), indicating greater difficulty in recovering the embedded interpretation. The study concludes that formal syntactic representations can be operationalized within Transformer-based NLP as an explicit interface between linguistic structure and contextual neural modeling, providing a controlled and interpretable approach to Arabic syntactic ambiguity resolution and beyond.

title: TRAC: Trajectory-aware Reuse and Adaptive Correction for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation
summary: Autoregressive (AR) video generation enables scalable long-video synthesis by sequentially generating fixed-length chunks, but incurs substantial computational cost from repeated denoising and attention over growing historical contexts. Recent cache reuse methods exploit temporal redundancy to reduce this cost, yet are mainly designed for single-trajectory generation, making them less suitable for sequentially coupled AR trajectories where approximation errors can accumulate and propagate across chunks. To address this challenge, we propose TRAC, a Trajectory-aware Reuse and Adaptive Correction framework for efficient and robust AR video generation. TRAC integrates three complementary components: (1) Robust Cumulative Scheduling (RCS), which selects cache reuse schedules by accounting for cumulative rollout errors and their variation across chunks and prompts; (2) Autoregressive Trajectory-aware Guidance Scheduling (ATGS), which coordinates classifier-free guidance refreshes along the global AR trajectory; and (3) Spectral Structure Correction (SSC), which adaptively restores low-frequency structural information to mitigate long-term error accumulation. By combining these innovations, TRAC substantially improves the efficiency-quality trade-off of AR video generation. For example, on VBench with SkyReels-V2, it achieves a 6.03x speedup over the vanilla model with only ~0.6% VBench score degradation, while consistently outperforming existing AR acceleration methods in both latency and generation quality. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/yolosjxhhhhhh/trac.

title: A Shortest Augmenting Path Algorithm for Linear Matroid Parity
summary:
The matroid parity problem generalizes both graph matching and matroid intersection. Although the general version is intractable, Lovász (1981) developed a polynomial-time algorithm for the linear matroid parity problem, assuming the availability of matrix representations. Subsequently, Gabow and Stallmann (1986) presented an augmenting path algorithm, which has long been recognized as one of the fastest deterministic algorithms. Since shortest augmenting paths improved algorithms for graph matching (Micali & Vazirani, 1980) and linear matroid intersection (Cunningham, 1986), extending these techniques to linear matroid parity appears to be a natural progression. However, such an algorithm has remained elusive for four decades.
  We present the first shortest augmenting path algorithm for linear matroid parity. Our approach synthesizes the augmenting path algorithm of Gabow and Stallmann with the synchronized blossom formation of Micali and Vazirani, whose correctness was recently proven by Vazirani (2024). Our key technical contributions are threefold: (i) a linear-algebraic argument that bounds the lengths of shortest augmenting paths for linear matroid parity, which generalizes Cunningham's bound for linear matroid intersection; (ii) an a priori characterization of shortest search paths through lower bounds on their lengths; and (iii) an extension of the structural properties for graph matching established by Izumi, Kitamura, and Yamaguchi (2025) to the linear matroid parity setting.
  Our algorithm deterministically solves the linear matroid parity problem in ${\rm O}(nr^2\log r)$ time, where $n$ is the ground set size and $r$ is the matroid rank. By incorporating fast matrix multiplication, this complexity can be further reduced to ${\rm O}(nr^2)$. These results improve upon the long-standing deterministic bounds of ${\rm O}(nr^3)$ and ${\rm O}(nr^ω)$.

title: ULTRADISCOVERY: Abductive Exploration in an Interconnected, Epistemically Open Universe
summary: Scientific discovery often begins when scattered clues call for a new way of describing the world. Such abductive exploration can require constructing the representation in which an explanation is stated, when the world is epistemically open, and composing evidence scattered across contexts, when it is structurally interconnected. Existing benchmarks rarely separate these two demands or control them independently. We introduce ULTRADISCOVERY, an interactive world of five domains in which an agent revises an initially successful theory and predicts the outcome of an unseen cross-domain intervention. A $2 \times 2$ design leaves the representation open or discloses it, and leaves the evidence distributed or aligns it, with the latent dynamics fixed. With the representation open, agents across eleven models often retract the axiom they were taught, and none introduces the unobserved entity or rewrites the variables that a replacement requires. Disclosure triples intervention requests and adds about one of the eighteen findings the world affords, and alignment adds less. Two vendor-harness systems carry discovery into more domains, and one of them rewrites the variables in Open episodes. No system makes the exact prediction within 200 paid actions. At larger budgets one exact prediction appears with both aids, while every Open episode remains inexact. The results locate the difficulty in the step from accumulating evidence to composing it into a representation that transfers.

title: KV$^2$: A Self-Refining KV Cache
summary: The memory footprint of the key-value (KV) cache constrains the practical use of long-context models, and it dominates cost when one prefilled context must later serve many different queries. In this reusable setting, query-agnostic compression trades cost against quality: lightweight estimators are cheap but less accurate, whereas full-context reconstruction scoring is more accurate yet reprocesses the entire prompt. We introduce KV$^2$, a query-agnostic KV-cache compression method based on selective reconstruction. KV$^2$ first uses a lightweight proxy scorer to identify informative in-context tokens, then reprocesses only this subset to compute final eviction scores. On RULER, Needle-in-a-Haystack, and LongBench, KV$^2$'s margin over baselines widens as the budget tightens: on RULER 16K at a 2% KV-cache budget it improves the average score over the next-best baseline by more than 40 percentage points, and on LongBench it attains the highest average across 2%-10% budgets at lower compression-stage runtime and peak memory than full-context reconstruction. Reusable KV-cache compression thus does not require reprocessing the full context. Our code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/KVsquared-0B97.

title: Beyond Entropy: Self-Diagnostic Multi-Role Token Optimization for Video Reasoning
summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards has substantially advanced multimodal reasoning, yet it remains fundamentally limited by ambiguous token-level credit assignment. While high-entropy token heuristics encourage possibility exploration, naively extending them to video reasoning tends to induce lengthy reasoning, as the model becomes overly reliant on high-entropy visual activations. Alternative approaches that rely on counterfactual-based visual token localization for credit assignment also tend to over-prioritize visual exploration at the expense of decisive reasoning cues for answer derivation, thereby exacerbating the interference from spurious visual nuances. Moreover, these methods employ static counterfactual strategies that fail to co-evolve with the policy during training. In this paper, we introduce DyCPO, a co-evolutionary framework that jointly optimizes reliable token selection and adaptive counterfactual intervention. It constructs a multi-role dependence metric to balance visual exploration and answer-relevance mining in token-wise contrastive learning, while suppressing exploration-only filler tokens and spurious visual noise. Rather than relying on static counterfactual priors, DyCPO dynamically derives counterfactual signals from the model's own successful and failed rollouts, enabling self-diagnostic analysis and co-evolution of the optimization objective with the policy. Extensive experiments on complex video reasoning and general video understanding benchmarks demonstrate consistent performance improvements, establishing DyCPO as a robust token-level credit assignment paradigm for multimodal reinforcement learning.

title: Video-Time Priors for EEG-fNIRS Emotion Regression on Familiar Videos
summary: Do viewer-specific physiological signals improve continuous emotion regression beyond the stimulus-driven response shared across viewers? We examine this question by predicting emotion ratings for new viewers watching videos that also appear in the training set. As a stimulus-only baseline, we define a video-time prior:the smoothed median of training labels for each video at each second. We then combine this prior, using a fixed fusion weight, with a graph-based model of electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) signals. On MER-PS 2026, five-fold cross-validation grouped by participant over 24 participants yields a mean absolute error (MAE) of 29.01 for fusion, compared with 29.06 for the prior alone. On an external cohort of four participants excluded from training, the corresponding MAEs are 27.72 and 28.04. In this cohort, most of the MAE reduction relative to a global-constant baseline comes from the prior, that is, from video identity and playback time alone.Fusion lowers MAE for three of the four held-out participants and for nine of the fifteen videos. The added value of physiological signals is therefore small and varies across participants and videos. Because the model uses physiological signals recorded after each prediction time, it supports only offline prediction. Generalization to unseen videos remains untested.

title: Assessing Acceptance and Privacy Preferences of Third-party Financial Data Sharing in Bipolar Disorder
comments: 13 pages, 5 figures, preregistration available at https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/5AKEB
summary: Bipolar disorder is strongly associated with financial instability. We examine how different interventions motivate individuals with bipolar disorder to share financial data with others. This approach can inform the development of tools for digital monitoring and intervention designed to promote financial stability in this population. 500 individuals with BD completed a pre-registered factorial vignette survey to examine level of comfort with hypothetical scenarios involving third-party financial interventions during symptomatic and euthymic periods. Scenario components were systematically varied between third-party actors, mood states, and intervention types. Participants rated sharing comfort on a 0-10 point scale. Multilevel models tested differences alongside clinical and financial histories, relational trust, and personality. Participants were most comfortable involving care partners in financial planning. They were more comfortable with temporary spending restrictions during symptomatic states than euthymic periods, underscoring the importance of accurate mood detection for intervention delivery. Prior financial help-seeking behavior and higher relational trust predicted greater comfort. Bankruptcy experience --- declared by 11.4% and considered by 31.7% --- was associated with increased comfort with spending restrictions. Individuals with psychiatric advance directives (8%) were significantly more comfortable sharing spending behaviors than those without. Comfort with financial interventions was higher among those with prior financial challenges or help-seeking histories. Participants distinguished between symptomatic and euthymic periods, favoring targeted, time-limited restrictions over general monitoring. These findings extend prior work on financial data sharing for illness self-management.
comment: 13 pages, 5 figures, preregistration available at https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/5AKEB

title: Asynchrony Is Nearly Free for Evolution Strategies on Long-Horizon LLM Agentic Tasks
summary: Synchronous policy updates can limit the efficiency of post-training for long-horizon LLM agents. When trajectories span multiple interaction turns, completion times can vary substantially, and synchronous update barriers leave faster workers idling, wasting compute resources. Asynchronous reinforcement learning addresses this inefficiency but introduces policy lag and off-policy optimization. Evolution strategies (ES) are a backpropagation-free alternative to gradient-based training, yet require many perturbed-policy evaluations and have remained largely synchronous in current LLM post-training. We introduce bounded-staleness asynchronous ES and investigate its training behavior under stale fitness measurements. On WebShop, we systematically vary the lag and fraction of stale fitness measurements and additionally introduce two stress tests to probe extreme staleness cases. Natural asynchrony closely tracks synchronous ES, and degradation in evaluation accuracy remains small even under extreme staleness, including when all fitness measurements are stale. These findings suggest that ES can tolerate substantial policy staleness without explicit off-policy correction, supporting its use in asynchronous post-training for long-horizon LLM agents.

title: D-DOIT: Training-free Adaptation of Discrete Diffusion via Doob's h-Transform
summary: We propose D-DOIT (Discrete Doob-Oriented Inference-time Transformation), a training-free and efficient adaptation method for discrete diffusion models with generic rewards. D-DOIT formulates adaptation as sampling from a reward-tilted target distribution and realizes this transport through Doob's h-transform of the discrete diffusion reverse kernel, using only reward values rather than reward gradients. Unlike continuous diffusion, masked discrete diffusion samples categorical token-reveal transitions rather than continuous state updates. D-DOIT derives the corresponding discrete Doob's h-transform, which guides sampling by reweighting reverse transition probabilities instead of adding a drift correction. To make this transformation practical, D-DOIT avoids expensive future rollouts. At each guided step, D-DOIT samples candidate next states, uses the model prediction head to complete each candidate into a clean sequence, evaluates each completion with the reward oracle, and resamples the next state with probabilities proportional to the rewards. An optional late-stage best-of-K refinement further improves sample quality by branching trajectories only near the end of denoising, avoiding the $K$-fold cost over the full trajectory. Empirically, across regulatory DNA design and protein inverse folding benchmarks, D-DOIT outperforms training-free guidance baselines. It improves enhancer activity and cell-type specificity while preserving sequence naturalness, and achieves the highest success rate in protein inverse folding.

title: E$^2$-OPSD: Taming Entropy Overshoot in On-Policy Self-Distillation
summary: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) provides dense token-level supervision without a second model: one network acts as teacher with the reference solution and as student with only the problem. We identify a specific failure mode of this recipe. During training, student token entropy rises past the teacher's and remains elevated, a pattern we call entropy overshoot. We trace it to both sides of distillation. The reference-conditioned teacher is confident along its answer-directed reasoning path, but this confidence transfers poorly to student-generated prefixes, making its supervision overly tied to answer-specific cues rather than reusable reasoning patterns; meanwhile, the forward KL used by OPSD continually diffuses the student's predictive distribution without pulling it back. We introduce E$^2$-OPSD to address both causes. Exemplar-guided teaching replaces the current answer with a retrieved solved neighboring problem, providing transferable reasoning guidance without revealing the destination and better matching student-reachable states. Entropy-aware distillation uses the student-teacher entropy gap to determine the direction and strength of each token's correction. E$^2$-OPSD improves math reasoning by up to 4.3 points in mean@16 over OPSD, while out-of-domain evaluations show gains over the corresponding base models of up to 4.9 points in mean@16 and 5.5 points in pass@8. Despite these gains, E$^2$-OPSD remains simple, requiring no additional forward passes or networks. Code repo: https://github.com/orionfei/E2-OPSD.

title: Order Matters: Competition-Guided Query Ordering for RNN-Based Object Detection
summary: DETR-style detectors use one-to-one bipartite matching during training to assign object queries to ground-truth objects, enabling end-to-end set prediction without non-maximum suppression (NMS). However, without an explicit de-duplication procedure, multiple queries can still produce highly similar hypotheses for the same object, making training unstable and predictions less decisive. Inspired by the sequential ordering of NMS, we propose DETRNN, a plug-and-play module that turns unordered object queries into a competition-aware sequence for recurrent refinement. DETRNN builds an explicit confidence-and-similarity based order from prior predictions, then refines queries with an RNN along this order to model competition inside the decoder. This ordered recurrent refinement reduces redundant predictions, stabilizes optimization, and improves final detection accuracy. Experiments on multiple DETR-style detectors show consistent gains with comparable efficiency. Code repository: https://github.com/nigelwoo2008-coder/DETRNN.

title: Towards Unbiased On-Policy Distillation for Block Diffusion Language Models
summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) has emerged as an effective post-training paradigm for language models, with recent efforts extending it to block diffusion language models (BDLMs). However, existing studies focus almost exclusively on small block sizes, leaving distillation into student models with larger blocks underexplored. In this work, we investigate this regime and reveal two critical optimization biases that induce severe training instability. First, mismatched block boundaries between teacher and student cause \textbf{\textit{context misalignment}}, providing distorted supervisory signals that misguide student decoding. Second, even under aligned contexts, an \textbf{\textit{intrinsic optimization bias}} in OPD, where the student tends to rapidly absorb high-support signals while lagging on low-support updates, drives a premature confidence surge that traps weaker students in catastrophic overconfidence collapse. To resolve these, we propose \mbox{\textbf{Un-OPD}}, an unbiased on-policy distillation framework with two novelties for stabilizing BDLM training. First, Un-OPD introduces a boundary-aware step filtering strategy that eliminates context-misaligned decoding steps. Second, Un-OPD proposes moderating optimization intensity at high-support positions via a support-rebalanced confidence calibration, thereby bypassing overconfidence collapse. Beyond stability, we also introduce a rollout reuse mechanism to reduce rollout generation overhead. Extensive experiments on math reasoning and code generation benchmarks show that Un-OPD consistently stabilizes training and delivers superior performance while reducing wall-clock training time by approximately half.

title: Every View Counts: View-Consistent Panoptic Quality for Multi-view Panoptic Segmentation
comments: 23 pages, 8 figures. Under review. Youngmin Lee and Byungha Ko contributed equally
summary: Multi-view panoptic segmentation assigns a semantic class and a scene-level instance ID to every pixel of an unordered set of images, and recent feed-forward 3D models predict these labels for the input views in a single forward pass. Their predictions, however, have been evaluated with the scene-level PQ (PQ^scene) borrowed from per-scene optimization methods, typically on rendered held-out views. PQ^scene tiles all views of a scene into a single image, so that a missed appearance or a change of ID lowers the score of the matched pair only in proportion to its area. We propose View-Consistent Panoptic Quality (VC-PQ), which extends PQ from a single image to a set of input views, counts equally every view in which an instance is visible, and penalizes a prediction that is not visible in the same views as its ground truth. A decomposition of VC-PQ attributes the score a method loses to mask accuracy, view consistency, and the matching threshold. A single additional parameter recovers the area weighting of tiling for comparison. Under a fixed evaluation protocol on ScanNet++ and ScanNetv2, recent feed-forward methods are evaluated with VC-PQ and PQ^scene, and the decomposition shows where each of them loses its score. Controlled perturbations of the ground truth show that VC-PQ responds to the number of views in which an instance is missed or changes ID, whereas PQ^scene responds to their area. The aim of this work is to make view consistency part of the evaluation of multi-view panoptic segmentation, with VC-PQ reported alongside PQ^scene. The evaluation code and the input sets of the protocol are available at https://github.com/Renem24/vcpq.
comment: 23 pages, 8 figures. Under review. Youngmin Lee and Byungha Ko contributed equally

title: Calibrated Evidence Inference With a Small, Permissively Licensed Open Model
comments: 22 pages, 2 figures, 15 tables. Code, results files and the paper's sources: https://github.com/johann-e-li/fiorillo. Model: https://doi.org/10.57967/hf/10722. Registration: https://osf.io/kaxmn/
summary: Systematic reviewers who use a model to read randomized trials need each answer and a measure of how far to trust it. If the model is calibrated, so that its stated probabilities match how often it is right, a reviewer can accept its confident answers and check the rest by hand. This paper fine-tunes Qwen3-4B-Base with low-rank adapters and a classification head for evidence inference (Lehman et al., 2019; DeYoung et al., 2020): given a trial's article and a prompt that names an intervention, a comparator and an outcome, classify the result as a significant increase, a significant decrease or no significant difference. The articles of Evidence Inference 2.0 come from the open-access subset of PubMed Central, which includes articles under non-commercial and no-derivatives licenses, so the released model was fine-tuned only on the 1,431 of 2,657 training articles under CC BY, CC0 or the public domain; it is released under the Apache License 2.0 and runs on a laptop. On the test split, its expected calibration error is 0.017 and its log loss is lower than that of Gemma 4 31B-it given the same input zero-shot, meeting criteria registered on the Open Science Framework before testing. Its macro-F1, 0.925, is above every published result on that split that I found, though those systems used other inputs, scoring rules and prompt filters, and the test labels are public. Accepting its 80 percent most confident answers leaves an error rate of 2.6 percent among them. Context ablations show that the answers depend on the article, but the title alone carries some signal, which an informative title or recall of the trial could explain.
comment: 22 pages, 2 figures, 15 tables. Code, results files and the paper's sources: https://github.com/johann-e-li/fiorillo. Model: https://doi.org/10.57967/hf/10722. Registration: https://osf.io/kaxmn/

title: Minimal Witness Reinforcement Learning
summary: ``What are the irreducible conditions that are sufficient to produce an outcome?'' is one of the most common questions that recur across computation and science. Its answers, the minimal sufficient witnesses, are what we mean by explanations, mechanisms and reasons. These problems usually ask for multiple minimal witnesses, yet standard RL methods may reveal only one solution or redundant ones. We formalize this problem as minimal-witness identification and introduce Minimal-Witness Reinforcement Learning (MWRL). MWRL takes the union of the sets certified by successful proposals sampled from the policy and credits each proposal for the coverage the group union would lose without that proposal. This credit assignment, derived directly from the problem definition, unifies the demands for minimality and recovery of alternatives from a single black-box verifier bit. Under this principle, we derive a value iteration planner that recovers the entire family of witnesses and a policy gradient method that can scale to large language models. Across different experimental settings, MWRL recovers most minimal witnesses, while other methods return redundant supersets or a single witness. By making witness families learnable from verifier feedback, MWRL expands the scope of reinforcement learning beyond single-solution optimization. Our code is available at https://github.com/TSUITUENYUE/MWRL.

title: Stronger Hardness for Submodular Maximization Subject to a Matroid Constraint
comments: 13 pages. This version adds a remark about the relationship between this work and the results of arXiv:2610.00545
summary: Maximizing a submodular function subject to a matroid constraint is a cornerstone problem in combinatorial optimization. The state-of-the-art algorithm for this problem obtains $0.401$-approximation~\cite{buchbinder2024constrained}, and the state-of-the-art hardness result shows that no polynomial time algorithm can obtain better than $0.478$-approximation for this problem~\cite{oveisgharan2011submodular}. In this work, we present the first improvement in $15$ years for the hardness result, showing that no polynomial time algorithm in the value-oracle model can obtain better than $8/17 \approx 0.471$-approximation, even for the special case of a cardinality or (simplified) partition matroid constraint.
comment: 13 pages. This version adds a remark about the relationship between this work and the results of arXiv:2610.00545

title: OTel: Open Telco AI Datasets, Benchmarks, and Models
summary: We present Open Telco (OTel), an open telecom AI resource that releases derived telecom datasets for retrieval, reranking, instruction tuning, and safety/abstention, together with 30 full-parameter post-trained baselines spanning 10 embedding models, 3 rerankers, and 17 language models. The community has already engaged substantially with the resource: as of May 3, 2026, the released models have been downloaded over 16 million times and the project has received 157+ pieces of media coverage worldwide. Building on prior open telecom datasets and benchmarks, OTel provides documented telecom data sources, held-out evaluation partitions, trained embedding models, rerankers, context-grounded LLMs, and safety/abstention data in one unified resource. Each baseline starts from an open-weight model and is post-trained on OTel-derived data using an open training recipe, then evaluated on held-out OTel evaluation partitions. OTel post-training improves performance across all three model families: embedding retrieval reaches 93.1% NDCG@10, reranking reaches 0.947 MRR@10, and language-model correctness reaches 87.8%. We release OTel as a reproducible starting point and invite the community to expand the data, improve embedding and reranking models, and build stronger context-grounded telecom LLMs.

title: SCOPE: Certified Theorem Proving with a Language Model as the Policy Planner
comments: Added code and data availability link in the Introduction
summary: In proof assistants such as Lean, a generated proof must pass machine compilation checks, so evaluation needs no human scoring. Direct generation fails on multi-step numeric propositions: a proof is valid only if every content integer is correct, so the pass rate is bounded by the k-th power of the per-integer accuracy. Controlled corruption across 2,617 reference proofs confirms this power law. SCOPE (State-Conditioned Operator Planning and Execution) enforces the natural division of labor: the model plans over an operator vocabulary, a symbolic engine executes the numerics, and a compiler renders the proof. On a 218-problem suite it certifies 191/218 (87.6%) with a 135M backbone; the 7B DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5-RL certifies 18/218 at 27.5 times the tokens and 37.5 times the wall-clock, and DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B certifies zero on a bidirectional dual suite. Multi-step thinking costs 6.12 discrete decision actions per problem and produces no natural-language thinking text. Replacing the lagged engine state in the decision frame with the current one lifts the pass rate from 117/218 to 191/218, while up-weighting the chain-end loss hurts. On the public Lean-Workbook library, 2,132 of 3,536 gradeable admissible problems certify (60.29%) with zero regression on the main suite. All readings come from a version-frozen review with independent rechecks and reverse verification. Restricting free generation and keeping decision-time information visible is a more direct route than enlarging the model.
comment: Added code and data availability link in the Introduction

title: CNet: A Complex-Valued Deep Learning Framework with Wirtinger Autodifferentiation and FFT--Hadamard Convolution
summary:
CNet is a C++/CUDA framework for deep complex-valued neural networks (CVNNs), trained by gradient descent with explicit Wirtinger (CR-calculus) derivatives. Complex models are underexplored yet natural where data is intrinsically complex -- RF/IQ, MRI k-space, radar/SAR, audio spectra -- and phase carries information real networks discard. CNet is physics-native: a network is a cascade of complex (often unitary) operations on an amplitude vector, and classification is a Born-rule measurement p_k = |z_k|^2 / ||z||^2 rather than a softmax over real logits. Every layer ships a CPU reference and a finite-difference-verified CUDA kernel; the static, batch-cloned computation graph captures cleanly into CUDA Graphs, outperforming eager and compiled torch.complex64 on an H100.
  We present three studies. (1) A fully complex causal language model, built on a new causal (triangular-masked) Fourier mixer with an O(N log N) Bluestein evaluation of the forward pass and its Wirtinger adjoint, matches a parameter-matched real causal FNet on character-level tiny-shakespeare in under half the steps. We introduce Born-rule attention, a content-based causal mixer whose weights are the quantum-measurement probabilities |<Q_k, K_j>|^2 -- to our knowledge the first classical, complex-valued attention to replace softmax with the squared-magnitude Born score; with rotary embeddings and per-token complex normalization it reaches 1.52 nats/char, matching softmax self-attention, and transfers unchanged to byte-level (1.31 nats/char) and sub-word WikiText-103. (2) On radio-modulation classification (RML2016.10a/RML22) we trace the pooled-power accuracy ceiling to discarded temporal structure and recover it with a learnable cyclostationary conjugate-lag operator. (3) A bottleneck analysis of the Fourier phase problem in coherent-diffraction imaging isolates where complex-valued networks still need new operators.

title: ParanoiaEval: Benchmarking Unnecessary Defensive Work in Agentic Coding
summary: As coding agents increasingly undertake real-world work autonomously, judging whether their risk treatments are warranted has become important. Existing work evaluates related agent behaviors from separate perspectives, but lacks a systematic framework for unifying these behaviors. To bridge this gap, we introduce ParanoiaEval, the first benchmark for unified evaluation of risk-treatment capabilities in coding agents. Grounded in the well-established Avoidance-Transfer-Mitigation-Acceptance framework in software engineering risk management, ParanoiaEval operationalizes its 4 fundamental treatments for coding-agent settings and contains 200 evidence-controlled repository-level task pairs, each differing only in treatment-defining evidence. We further introduce dedicated metrics for risk-treatment violations and evidence responsiveness, using a human-calibrated agentic judge for reliable evaluation. Large-scale experiments on 8 representative models and a post-hoc human study reveal that (I) unnecessary risk treatment occurs in 11.2%-58.7% of runs despite explicit evidence, with substantial variation across agent configurations; (II) stronger task capability does not ensure more appropriate risk treatment, while treatment violations substantially harm developers' experience, establishing risk treatment as an independent capability dimension; and (III) agents exhibit systematic patterns consistent with established risk-management findings, suggesting that knowledge from human practice can guide the diagnosis and improvement of this capability.

title: LASER: Latent Space Adjoint Matching for Support-Constrained Entropy-Regularized Offline RL
summary: While offline reinforcement learning (RL) enables policy optimization from static datasets without costly online interaction, it remains bottlenecked by the risk of executing out-of-distribution (OOD) actions. Recent approaches mitigate this by learning a behavior-cloning policy through flow matching and then performing RL within its constrained latent space. However, naively optimizing the latent policy can easily cause the policy to collapse into a brittle mode or exploit sharp artifacts of the learned critic. In this work, we find that entropy regularization is essential in latent-space RL for addressing these challenges. We introduce LASER, a novel offline RL algorithm that applies latent-space adjoint matching to achieve entropy-regularized latent-space RL with expressive flow policies while avoiding backpropagation through time. Through comprehensive experiments on 40 challenging OGBench tasks with varying dataset qualities, we show that LASER achieves state-of-the-art performance. Notably, LASER uses fixed method-specific hyperparameters across all tasks and outperforms the evaluated baselines, including those with task- and dataset-specific tuning, which highlights the robust applicability of LASER. Project website: https://mit-realm.github.io/laser/.

title: Trust a Few: The Weakest Assumptions a Protocol Needs
summary: Protocol verifiers check whether a protocol meets a security goal under stated trust assumptions, such as that a key is never leaked, a value is fresh, or a channel is authentic. They do not say which of those assumptions the goal needs. Rowe, Guttman and Liskov asked for the weakest assumptions under which a protocol achieves a goal and left the question open. We answer it for assumptions about keys, values and channels. Call a run that violates the goal an attack, and the assumptions that would rule it out its stopping set. The least a protocol must trust to meet a goal is exactly the set of minimal ways to stop all of its minimal attacks. Several such sets may exist. The answer becomes unique once either/or assumptions are allowed, and it is a single set exactly when every minimal attack is stopped by a single assumption. A Galois connection between assumptions and goals explains why: a goal may end in "or", but its hypothesis may not. The same structure gives the trust needed by a conjunction of goals and an exact condition under which composed protocols need no extra trust. To compute the answer, a loop asks a verifier whether a candidate suffices, records what stops each attack it reports, and recomputes the candidates. Deciding whether some trust of at most k assumptions suffices is NP-hard. With a bounded analyser of our own and with CPSA, the loop finds the weakest trust for 18 goals over ten protocols and their variants, and on each it agrees with evaluating every trust using the same verifier. The answers include an assumption that our model of the adopted fix of Kerberos PKINIT states but the client's authentication of the server does not need, and channel assumptions under which Needham-Schroeder meets its goal in a bounded model.

title: Identifiability of a dissipative knowledge-dynamics model: exact recovery under designed excitation, degeneration on observational data
comments: Corrected the implicit integration scheme and Proposition 4; revised Lemma 1; specified the practice input, difficulty reference, rank and training split; added an ablation, a replay of the real schedule with known rates, and a positive control of the validation protocol (Section 7.6); moderated claims; added relation to companion work and an AI-use declaration
summary: Human learning is a dissipative dynamical process: mastery accumulates through practice, decays through forgetting, and propagates across interdependent concepts. We model it as a nonlinear dissipative system of ordinary differential equations whose parameters are mechanistically meaningful (a transfer-of-practice matrix, per-concept forgetting rates, and a saturating practice-response gain), and we study when those parameters can actually be recovered from data. For two concepts, we prove a constructive structural identifiability theorem for the associated inverse problem under explicit excitation conditions, together with monotonicity, robustness and L-stability results. We derive an implicit L-stable scheme and a batched solver numerically equivalent to the per-trajectory formulation yet two orders of magnitude faster. The empirical study is two-sided. Under the theorem's excitation conditions, synthetic recovery is exact. On large observational benchmarks it is not. An apparently strong recovery, with forgetting rates correlating with topic error rates at Spearman $ρ= 0.83$, is refuted by four controls: it survives destroying the temporal order of the data, is matched by a classical Bayesian baseline, and is unaffected by removing real timestamps. A single shared forgetting rate attains the same accuracy, and replaying the real schedule with identical true rates reproduces most of the correlation. A positive control shows that the controls detect forgetting where it is observable. We trace the effect to the stationary structure of the model and show that it is consistent with the degeneration anticipated by the theory in the absence of designed excitation.
comment: Corrected the implicit integration scheme and Proposition 4; revised Lemma 1; specified the practice input, difficulty reference, rank and training split; added an ablation, a replay of the real schedule with known rates, and a positive control of the validation protocol (Section 7.6); moderated claims; added relation to companion work and an AI-use declaration

AI.title_translation: 耗散知识动力学模型的可辨识性：设计激励下的精确恢复与观测数据上的退化
AI.tldr: 非线性耗散知识动力学模型在理论设计的激励下能精确恢复参数，但在真实观测数据中由于缺乏主动激励，参数估计会严重退化并产生虚假相关性。
AI.motivation: 人类学习是一个耗散动力学过程，包含练习积累、遗忘衰减及概念间迁移。为了明确机理模型中的物理参数（如遗忘率、迁移强度）何时能够真正从数据中反演识别，探讨可辨识性的理论边界及在实际观测数据下的有效性。
AI.method: 将人类学习建模为包含练习迁移矩阵、遗忘率和饱和增益的非线性耗散常微分方程（ODE）系统；针对双概念情形，证明了具有明确激励条件的结构可辨识性定理，并建立单调性、鲁棒性与L-稳定性结果；推导了隐式L-稳定格式和速度提升两个数量级的批量求解器；设计了多项严苛的消融和反事实对照实验以检验参数真实恢复程度。
AI.result: 在满足理论激发条件时，合成数据上的参数恢复完全精确；但在大规模真实观测基准上，恢复发生退化：表面上遗忘率与主题错误率达到0.83的高相关性被打乱时序、移除时间戳、共享单一遗忘率及贝叶斯基线等4项对照实验所证伪，表明该相关性为非时序性的统计假象。
AI.conclusion: 在缺乏专门设计的激励条件时，该模型在真实观测数据上的参数恢复会发生退化，观测到的虚假强相关性源于模型的稳态结构，这与理论预期的退化现象一致。
AI.translation: 人类学习是一个耗散动力学过程：掌握度通过练习积累，通过遗忘衰减，并在相互依赖的概念之间传播。我们将其建模为一个非线性耗散常微分方程系统，其参数具有明确的机制含义（练习迁移矩阵、各概念的遗忘率以及饱和练习响应增益），并研究这些参数何时能够真正从数据中恢复。对于两个概念的情形，我们证明了在显式激励条件下相关逆问题的构造性结构可辨识性定理，同时给出了单调性、鲁棒性和L-稳定性结果。我们推导了一种隐式L-稳定格式和一种批量求解器，在数值上与按轨迹求解的表述等价，但速度提升了两个数量级。实证研究具有两面性：在定理给出的激励条件下，合成数据的恢复是精确的；而在大规模观测基准上则不然。表面上强劲的恢复效果（遗忘率与主题错误率的斯皮尔曼相关系数达 ρ = 0.83）被四组对照实验所驳斥：该相关性在破坏数据时间顺序后依然存在，与经典贝叶斯基线相吻合，且不受去除真实时间戳的影响；单一共享遗忘率即可达到相同的准确率，而使用相同真实遗忘率重放真实日程也能重现大部分相关性。正对照实验表明，对照组在可观测时能够检测到遗忘。我们将该效应归结于模型的稳态结构，并表明这与在缺乏专门设计激励时理论所预期的退化现象相一致。
AI.summary: 本文研究了一个非线性耗散知识动力学ODE模型的结构可辨识性。理论上，论文证明了在特定激励条件下参数可精确恢复，并开发了高效的L-稳定隐式求解器。实验表明，尽管合成数据能完美恢复参数，但在真实观测数据上模型参数恢复严重退化，表面上的高相关性被多项严格对照实验证伪，揭示了无设计激励下观测数据难以辨识真实动态参数的本质局限。
AI.keywords: 知识动力学, 耗散系统, 结构可辨识性, 参数恢复, 观测数据退化
AI.comments: 该研究的一大创新与亮点在于将控制论中的结构可辨识性理论严格引入知识追踪与学习动力学建模中，不仅给出了精确恢复的充分激发条件，还通过严谨的反事实对照实验（如打乱时序、移除时间戳等），揭示了观测数据上看似显著的相关性实为虚假信号。这指出了当前基于观测基准评估动态认知模型参数时普遍存在的退化陷阱，对教育数据挖掘与动力系统辨识具有重要警示和指导意义。

title: Defining Purpose-Limited Secrets
summary: A cryptographic secret is issued for a purpose but grants a capability, and the capability is usually larger. Deployed systems state the purpose in policy and enforce only the capability. We make the purpose a property of the secret. A mechanism sees operations, not reasons, so a scheme enforces an admissible set $A(P)$ of operations that stands in for a declared intended use $I$; whether $I$ captures the human purpose is a modeling obligation that marks where policy takes over. Against the same $I$ we define three regimes: under confinement an operation outside the intended use is infeasible, under mediation a trusted component refuses it, and under accountability use beyond a stated bound is possible but attributed to the holder. The confinement games, for unpredictability and indistinguishability, coincide with the key-query forms of functional-signature unforgeability and constrained-PRF pseudorandomness and correspond to simulation-secure functional encryption within its feasibility boundary; stated against $I$, they also register a predicate that permits too much. A payment token uses all three regimes on one secret: it pays one capped charge at one merchant, can be narrowed but not widened, is checked by the merchant, and identifies the withdrawing account if spent twice. Attenuation unforgeability reduces to unforgeable signatures and a collision-resistant hash without random oracles; traceability and non-frameability hold under discrete log and unforgeable signatures in the random-oracle model. We present this framework as a common specification against which existing primitives are stated and compared.

AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种将目的作为秘密属性的加密框架，并定义了三种使用限制机制（限制、中介、问责），以确保加密秘密的使用不超出其声明的预期用途。
AI.motivation: 现有的加密秘密通常为了特定目的而发放，但其赋予的能力往往超出该目的，且部署的系统仅强制执行能力而非目的，导致潜在的过度授权。
AI.method: 本文将目的作为秘密的一个属性。提出了一种机制，通过定义一个可接受操作集A(P)来代表声明的预期用途I。在此基础上，定义了三种使用限制机制：限制（confinement）、中介（mediation）和问责（accountability）。还提出了针对这些机制的博弈和安全规约。
AI.result: 限制博弈与功能签名不可伪造性和受限PRF伪随机性相符，并对应于功能加密。衰减不可伪造性可简化为不可伪造签名和抗碰撞哈希。可追溯性和不可陷害性在离散对数和不可伪造签名假设下成立。一个支付令牌的例子展示了三种机制的应用。
AI.conclusion: 本文提出了一个通用的规范框架，用于表述和比较现有的加密原语，以实现目的受限的秘密。
AI.translation: 加密秘密为特定目的而发行，但通常会赋予更大的能力。部署的系统在策略中声明目的，但仅强制执行能力。我们使目的成为秘密的一个属性。由于机制只看到操作，而非原因，因此一个方案会强制执行一个代表声明的预期用途I的允许操作集A(P)；I是否捕捉到人类目的，是一个建模义务，标志着策略接管的边界。针对相同的I，我们定义了三种机制：在限制（confinement）下，超出预期用途的操作是不可行的；在中介（mediation）下，受信任组件会拒绝该操作；在问责（accountability）下，超出规定范围的使用是可能的，但会被归因于持有者。限制博弈，包括不可预测性和不可区分性，与功能签名不可伪造性和受限PRF伪随机性的密钥查询形式一致，并在其可行性范围内对应于模拟安全的功能加密；针对I表述时，它们也记录了一个允许过多的谓词。一个支付令牌在一个秘密上使用了所有这三种机制：它在一个商家处支付一次封顶费用，可以缩小但不能扩大，由商家检查，并在重复消费时识别取款账户。衰减不可伪造性在没有随机预言机的情况下可简化为不可伪造签名和抗碰撞哈希；在随机预言机模型中，可追溯性和不可陷害性在离散对数和不可伪造签名下成立。我们将此框架作为一个通用规范，用于表述和比较现有原语。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一个用于定义“目的受限秘密”的密码学框架，旨在解决现有加密秘密赋予能力超出其声明目的的问题。通过将目的作为秘密的固有属性，并引入限制、中介和问责三种使用机制，确保秘密的使用严格符合预期用途。该框架提供了一种统一的规范，用于分析和比较现有的加密原语，并展示了其在支付令牌等实际应用中的潜力。
AI.keywords: 目的受限秘密, 加密, 细粒度控制, 功能加密, 安全框架
AI.comments: 这篇论文通过将“目的”直接嵌入到加密秘密的属性中，提供了一个新颖且重要的视角，以解决加密系统中能力过度授权的根本问题。其提出的限制、中介和问责三种机制，为细粒度的秘密控制提供了理论基础和实践指导。这对于构建更安全、更符合意图的加密系统具有重要意义，尤其是在隐私保护和合规性要求日益严格的背景下。

title: Efficient Heuristics and Machine Learning Approach for Fault Characterization in Distributed Self-Stabilizing Programs
summary: Modern large-scale systems rely on distributed protocols to maximize efficiency while preserving the correctness guarantees of single-process execution. However, designing such protocols is non-trivial: adding resources to a system inherently increases its complexity, which in turn introduces faults that must be addressed during design. One such fault class, arising in systems that use distributed shared memory (e.g., replicated databases), is consistency violating fault (cvf), a fault in which a process accessing shared memory reads stale data previously written by another process. Cvfs are inherent to systems that prioritize availability over strict consistency. Prior work has shown that self-stabilizing programs remain correct under high availability, provided such faults stay within a tolerable bound. Characterizing the behavior of self-stabilizing programs in the presence of cvfs can therefore help system designers build systems that are both correct and efficient. In this paper, we study self-stabilizing programs under cvfs to understand when and where such faults occur, enabling runtime measures that improve computational efficiency. Since exhaustive state-space exploration does not scale, it suffers from state-space explosion; our study investigates two complementary approaches: a conflict-based state-space exploration technique for monotonically stabilizing $(Δ + 1)$-Graph Coloring programs, and a machine-learning-based approach for a Maximal Independent Set program. We propose a conflicting-edges-based state-space exploration algorithm alongside a rigorously validated ML model, evaluated on an out-of-distribution dataset through structural consistency checks against known graph invariants.

AI.title_translation: 分布式自稳定程序中故障特征化的高效启发式和机器学习方法
AI.tldr: 本文研究分布式自稳定程序中的一致性违反故障 (cvf)，采用基于冲突的状态空间探索和机器学习方法来表征故障行为，以提高计算效率。
AI.motivation: 现代大型分布式系统高度复杂，容易出现一致性违反故障 (cvf)。在自稳定程序中表征这些故障对于设计正确且高效的系统至关重要，特别是当穷举状态空间探索因状态空间爆炸而不可行时。
AI.method: 本文研究了两种互补的方法：1. 针对单调自稳定 (Δ + 1)-图着色程序的基于冲突的状态空间探索技术，包括提出的一种基于冲突边的状态空间探索算法。2. 针对最大独立集程序的基于机器学习的方法，涉及一个经过严格验证的机器学习模型，该模型通过对已知图不变量进行结构一致性检查，在分布外数据集上进行评估。
AI.result: 这些方法旨在了解自稳定程序中一致性违反故障 (cvf) 发生的时间和地点，从而实现提高计算效率的运行时措施。机器学习模型通过结构一致性检查，在分布外数据集上进行了严格验证。
AI.conclusion: 通过使用高效启发式和机器学习研究一致性违反故障下的自稳定程序，本文提供了表征故障行为的方法，有助于系统设计者构建更正确和高效的分布式系统。
AI.translation: 现代大规模系统依赖分布式协议来最大限度地提高效率，同时保持单进程执行的正确性保证。然而，设计此类协议并非易事：向系统添加资源会固有地增加其复杂性，这反过来又会引入必须在设计过程中解决的故障。一类此类故障，出现在使用分布式共享内存（例如，复制数据库）的系统中，是一致性违反故障 (cvf)，即进程访问共享内存时读取先前由另一个进程写入的陈旧数据。Cvfs 是优先考虑可用性而非严格一致性的系统所固有的。先前的研究表明，如果此类故障保持在可容忍的范围内，自稳定程序在高可用性下仍能保持正确性。因此，表征存在 cvfs 的自稳定程序的行为可以帮助系统设计者构建既正确又高效的系统。在本文中，我们研究了 cvfs 下的自稳定程序，以了解此类故障何时何地发生，从而实现提高计算效率的运行时措施。由于穷举状态空间探索不具可扩展性，它会遭受状态空间爆炸；我们的研究调查了两种互补的方法：针对单调自稳定 (Δ + 1)-图着色程序的基于冲突的状态空间探索技术，以及针对最大独立集程序的基于机器学习的方法。我们提出了一种基于冲突边的状态空间探索算法，以及一个经过严格验证的机器学习模型，通过对已知图不变量进行结构一致性检查，在分布外数据集上进行了评估。
AI.summary: 本文解决了分布式自稳定程序中一致性违反故障 (cvfs) 的表征难题，这类故障常见于优先考虑可用性的大规模系统。鉴于穷举状态空间探索的不可行性，作者提出了两种互补方法：一种是针对图着色程序的基于冲突的状态空间探索技术，另一种是针对最大独立集程序的机器学习方法。这些方法旨在识别 cvfs 发生的时间和地点，最终实现计算效率的运行时改进。机器学习模型的验证包括对分布外数据集进行结构一致性检查。
AI.keywords: 分布式系统, 自稳定, 故障表征, 一致性违反故障, 机器学习, 状态空间探索
AI.comments: 本文解决了分布式系统设计中的一个重要问题，结合了传统算法启发式方法和现代机器学习技术，以克服状态空间爆炸问题。针对不同程序类型（图着色和最大独立集）采用互补方法，表明了全面的策略。对机器学习模型在分布外数据集上进行的严格验证，表明了评估的稳健性。

title: AdaptEvo: Learning under Imperfect Supervision through Confidence-Adaptive Training with Knowledge Evolution
comments: 22 pages, 4 figures; team authorship with the full author list and affiliations in Contributors; results unchanged
summary: Rule-governed contextual decision tasks require models to apply specified rules to case-specific context and evidence. Written rules can leave gaps in decision guidance and process evaluation, while reference judgments vary in their support from the rules and evidence. To address these challenges, we introduce AdaptEvo, a framework for learning under imperfect supervision that couples confidence-adaptive policy optimization with evolving decision knowledge and evaluation rubrics. Its Training module uses Confidence-Adaptive GRPO (CA-GRPO) to balance outcome and process rewards according to reference confidence. Its Evolution module synthesizes reusable decision knowledge from recurring failures across training cases and refines process rubrics to detect overlooked errors. To support empirical evaluation, we construct an industrial multimodal content moderation dataset comprising a training set and In-Period and Out-of-Period test sets, with the latter collected under changed rules. Using Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, AdaptEvo achieves 61.9% exact-label accuracy and 72.2% binary decision accuracy on In-Period, exceeding GRPO by 7.5 and 3.7 percentage points, respectively. On Out-of-Period, the policy trained with CA-GRPO retains exact-label accuracy gains over the base model across evaluated checkpoints without injected decision knowledge, while GRPO declines with continued training. CA-GRPO also outperforms the tested fixed reward mixtures on both Out-of-Period metrics.

AI.title_translation: AdaptEvo：通过结合知识演进的置信度自适应训练在不完美监督下学习
AI.tldr: 提出了一种名为AdaptEvo的框架，通过置信度自适应训练和知识演进解决不完美监督下的决策问题，在内容审核任务中取得了显著性能提升。
AI.motivation: 规则制定的上下文决策任务中存在监督不完美（如书面规则有漏洞、参考判断支持度不一）的挑战，现有方法难以很好地平衡结果与过程奖励及适应规则变化。
AI.method: 提出了AdaptEvo框架，包含使用置信度自适应GRPO（CA-GRPO）的训练模块，以及从重复失败中合成可复用决策知识和精炼过程标准的演进模块。
AI.result: 在工业多模态内容审核数据集上，AdaptEvo在In-Period测试集上达到了61.9%的精确标签准确率和72.2%的二元决策准确率，超越GRPO；在Out-of-Period测试集上也保持了更好的鲁棒性。
AI.conclusion: AdaptEvo框架通过置信度自适应训练与知识演进，有效解决了不完美监督和规则变化带来的挑战，在内容 moderation 任务中显著优于传统方法。
AI.translation: 规则支配的上下文决策任务要求模型将指定的规则应用于特定案例的上下文和证据中。书面规则在决策指导和过程评估中可能会留下空白，而参考判断受规则和证据支持的程度也各不相同。为了应对这些挑战，我们引入了AdaptEvo，这是一个用于不完美监督下学习的框架，它将置信度自适应策略优化与不断演进的决策知识和评估标准结合起来。其训练模块使用置信度自适应GRPO（CA-GRPO）根据参考置信度平衡结果和过程奖励。其演进模块从训练案例中反复出现的失败中综合可复用的决策知识，并精炼过程标准以检测被忽视的错误。为了支持实证评估，我们构建了一个工业多模态内容审核数据集，包含训练集以及In-Period和Out-of-Period测试集，后者是在规则变更的情况下收集的。使用Qwen3.6-35B-A3B，AdaptEvo在In-Period上取得了61.9%的精确标签准确率和72.2%的二元决策准确率，分别比GRPO高出7.5和3.7个百分点。在Out-of-Period上，使用CA-GRPO训练的策略在评估的各个检查点上都保持了对基础模型的精确标签准确率提升（无需注入决策知识），而GRPO随着持续训练而下降。CA-GRPO在两个Out-of-Period指标上也优于测试的固定奖励混合方案。
AI.summary: AdaptEvo是一个用于不完美监督下学习的框架，它将置信度自适应策略优化（CA-GRPO）与不断演进的决策知识和评估标准相结合，在内容审核任务中表现出优异的准确性和对规则变化的适应能力。
AI.keywords: 不完美监督, 置信度自适应训练, 知识演进, 多模态内容审核, 策略优化
AI.comments: 该论文针对不完美监督下的上下文决策任务，提出了一种新颖的AdaptEvo框架，结合了置信度自适应策略优化和演进的决策知识与评估标准，展现了在规则变化场景下的强大鲁棒性和准确性。

title: Almost $L^\infty$-stability of the Ritz projection for the integral fractional Laplacian with $0<s\leq \tfrac12$
summary: For $0<s\leq 1/2$ and $d\geq 1$, the $\widetilde H^s$-projection onto piecewise linear finite element spaces on quasi-uniform meshes of a bounded Lipschitz domain in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a uniform exterior ball condition is almost stable in the maximum norm. The mesh domain need not coincide with the original domain.

AI.tldr: 对于$0<s	ext{≤} 1/2$，积分分数拉普拉斯算子的Ritz投影在有限元空间上几乎是$L^	ext{无穷}$稳定的。

AI.conclusion: 该论文证明了在特定参数范围和有限元设置下，积分分数拉普拉斯算子的Ritz投影具有几乎$L^	ext{无穷}$稳定性。

AI.summary: 本论文研究了积分分数拉普拉斯算子在$0<s	ext{≤} 1/2$和$d	ext{≥} 1$条件下的Ritz投影的稳定性。结果表明，将$	ext{widetilde H}^s$-投影应用于在准均匀网格上的分段线性有限元空间时，在最大范数下几乎是稳定的，并且网格域可以与原始域不重合。
AI.keywords: 积分分数拉普拉斯算子, Ritz投影, $L^	ext{无穷}$-稳定性, 有限元方法, $	ext{widetilde H}^s$-投影
AI.comments: 该论文解决了分数阶算子数值方法中的一个重要数学性质（稳定性）问题，特别是对于积分分数拉普拉斯算子。其“几乎$L^	ext{无穷}$稳定性”是一个有力的结果，考虑到分数阶算子和最大范数分析的复杂性。网格域的灵活性也值得关注。

title: NosRacer: Dynamic Detection of Race Conditions in On-Device Network Operating Systems
comments: 18 pages, 5 figures, 6 tables. Accepted to SIGOPS ATC 2026
summary:
Commercial on-device network operating systems (NOSes) run the complex control planes of production routers and switches, where configuration update tasks are executed by multiple loosely coupled components through asynchronous message passing. Such executions are prone to race conditions: the same ordered input commands may produce different outcomes when messages are delivered in different orders. The race conditions are difficult to expose because they often manifest only as subtle, delayed malfunctions. Existing static analysis techniques lack scalability and precision for large-scale industrial NOSes, while dynamic ones incur substantial system-execution cost when attempting to cover the space of asynchronous message interleavings.
  To address the challenges above, we present NosRacer, a dynamic analysis framework for race condition detection in industrial-grade on-device NOSes. NosRacer uses a two-phase design. The concentration phase reduces analysis scope by leveraging the locality of configuration update tasks. Race condition detection is then limited to a small subset of involved components and crucial state variables, thereby reducing the detection cost. The perturbation phase proactively perturbs message asynchrony to increase the likelihood of executions with race-condition-exposing message interleavings. It keeps perturbation practical by grouping compatible perturbations for parallel execution and adaptively strengthening perturbations.
  We implement NosRacer in a commercial, actively developed NOS. NosRacer is integrated into the existing testing factory and used to detect race conditions in 5 key control-plane components. NosRacer achieves 66% precision and detects 21 race conditions confirmed by developers as severe bugs, while keeping the detection overhead below 10%.
comment: 18 pages, 5 figures, 6 tables. Accepted to SIGOPS ATC 2026

AI.title_translation: NosRacer：设备内网络操作系统中竞态条件的动态检测
AI.tldr: NosRacer是一个高效的动态分析框架，通过集中化分析范围和主动扰动消息异步性，在工业级网络操作系统中低开销地检测出了多个严重的竞态条件。
AI.motivation: 商业设备内网络操作系统（NOS）通过异步消息传递执行配置更新任务，极易产生难以暴露且表现为微妙延迟故障的竞态条件。现有的静态分析缺乏扩展性和精度，而传统动态分析则面临巨大的系统执行开销。
AI.method: 提出了一个两阶段的动态分析框架NosRacer：1）集中阶段（concentration phase），利用配置更新任务的局部性缩减分析范围；2）扰动阶段（perturbation phase），通过分组并行执行和自适应增强来主动扰动消息异步性以暴露竞态。
AI.result: 在商业NOS的5个关键控制平面组件中进行集成测试，NosRacer实现了66%的精度，检测出了21个被开发人员确认为严重漏洞的竞态条件，同时将检测开销保持在10%以下。
AI.conclusion: NosRacer成功应用于商业NOS的控制平面组件测试中，以较低的开销高效地发现了大量严重的竞态条件漏洞，验证了其有效性和工业可行性。
AI.translation:
商业设备内网络操作系统（NOSes）运行着生产路由器和交换机的复杂控制平面，其中的配置更新任务由多个通过异步消息传递松散耦合的组件执行。此类执行极易产生竞态条件：当消息以不同顺序交付时，相同的有序输入命令可能会产生不同的结果。这些竞态条件很难暴露，因为它们通常只表现为微妙、延迟的故障。现有的静态分析技术对于大规模工业NOS缺乏可扩展性和精度，而动态分析技术在试图覆盖异步消息交织空间时会产生巨大的系统执行成本。
为了应对上述挑战，我们提出了NosRacer，这是一个用于工业级设备内NOS中竞态条件检测的动态分析框架。NosRacer采用两阶段设计。集中阶段通过利用配置更新任务的局部性来减少分析范围。然后，竞态条件检测被限制在参与组件和关键状态变量的小子集上，从而降低了检测成本。扰动阶段主动扰动消息的异步性，以增加具有暴露竞态条件的消息交织的执行可能性。它通过对兼容扰动进行分组以进行并行执行并自适应地加强扰动，从而使扰动保持实用性。
我们在一个商业的、积极开发的NOS中实现了NosRacer。NosRacer被集成到现有的测试工厂中，用于检测5个关键控制平面组件中的竞态条件。NosRacer实现了66%的精度，检测出了21个被开发人员确认为严重漏洞的竞态条件，同时将检测开销保持在10%以下。
AI.summary: 论文介绍了NosRacer，这是一个针对工业级设备内网络操作系统中竞态条件的动态检测框架。它通过集中阶段缩减分析范围和扰动阶段主动暴露消息异步性，以低系统开销成功检测出了多个严重的控制平面竞态条件。
AI.keywords: 网络操作系统, 竞态条件, 动态分析, 异步消息传递, 控制平面
AI.comments: 该论文针对工业级设备内网络操作系统（NOS）中的控制平面并发竞态条件问题，提出了一种创新的两阶段动态检测框架NosRacer。通过局部性分析缩减检测范围，并利用主动扰动机制在保持低开销的同时有效暴露竞态，具有很高的工业实用价值。

title: AdaptLSTM: Efficient Adaptive Online Learning for Cloud Workload Forecasting under Distribution Drift
summary: Accurate workload forecasting is critical for elastic resource provisioning in web-scale cloud services, where distribution shifts driven by viral content, product launches, and user behavior degrade offline-trained models rapidly. Naive online learning recovers accuracy but incurs prohibitive per-step compute cost. We propose AdaptLSTM, an adaptive online framework that detects drift via validation-calibrated thresholds and applies selective, targeted updates. On the Alibaba Machine Trace, AdaptLSTM recovers 54\% of Naive Online's improvement at 20\% cost ($2.7\times$ efficiency, $p=0.002$ over 10 seeds). On the more volatile Container Trace, it achieves 96\% at 20\% cost ($4.8\times$ efficiency, $+75\%$ MAE reduction over Static). Unlike classical drift detectors (ADWIN, DDM, Page-Hinkley) which fail to trigger on regression-scale error streams, AdaptLSTM fires 42 times over 301 steps and outperforms matched-budget baselines. Wall-clock profiling shows $1.33\times$ throughput gain and 45\% update-time reduction. The framework is model-agnostic: identical Pareto patterns hold for LSTM, GRU, and Transformer backbones.

AI.title_translation: AdaptLSTM：在分布漂移下用于云工作负载预测的高效自适应在线学习
AI.tldr: AdaptLSTM是一种自适应在线学习框架，通过检测分布漂移并选择性地更新模型，在云工作负载预测中实现了高效率和准确性，显著优于传统方法。
AI.motivation: 由于病毒式内容、产品发布和用户行为导致的分布变化，离线训练模型在网络规模云服务中会迅速失效，而朴素在线学习虽然能恢复准确性但计算成本过高。因此，需要一种高效的自适应在线学习方法来准确预测云工作负载。
AI.method: 提出AdaptLSTM框架，通过验证校准阈值检测分布漂移，并应用选择性的、有针对性的更新。该框架与模型无关，可用于LSTM、GRU和Transformer骨干网络。
AI.result: 在阿里巴巴机器轨迹数据集上，AdaptLSTM以20%的成本恢复了朴素在线学习54%的改进（2.7倍效率）。在更不稳定的容器轨迹数据集上，以20%的成本实现了96%的改进（4.8倍效率），MAE比静态模型减少75%。与传统漂移检测器（如ADWIN、DDM、Page-Hinkley）不同，AdaptLSTM在301步中触发了42次。墙钟分析显示吞吐量提高1.33倍，更新时间减少45%。
AI.conclusion: AdaptLSTM通过自适应在线学习，在存在分布漂移的云工作负载预测中，以显著提高的效率和准确性优于现有方法，并且具有模型无关性。
AI.translation: 准确的工作负载预测对于网络规模云服务中的弹性资源调配至关重要，其中由病毒式内容、产品发布和用户行为驱动的分布变化会迅速降低离线训练模型的性能。朴素在线学习可以恢复准确性，但会产生过高的每步计算成本。我们提出了AdaptLSTM，一个自适应在线框架，它通过验证校准阈值检测漂移并应用选择性的、有针对性的更新。在阿里巴巴机器轨迹数据集上，AdaptLSTM以20%的成本恢复了朴素在线学习54%的改进（2.7倍效率，$p=0.002$，基于10个种子）。在更不稳定的容器轨迹数据集上，它以20%的成本实现了96%的改进（4.8倍效率，比静态模型MAE减少75%）。与在回归规模错误流上无法触发的经典漂移检测器（ADWIN、DDM、Page-Hinkley）不同，AdaptLSTM在301步中触发了42次，并优于匹配预算的基线。墙钟分析显示吞吐量提高1.33倍，更新时间减少45%。该框架与模型无关：相同的帕累托模式适用于LSTM、GRU和Transformer骨干网络。
AI.summary: AdaptLSTM是一个用于云工作负载预测的自适应在线学习框架，旨在解决由于分布漂移导致的离线训练模型性能下降和朴素在线学习成本过高的问题。它通过验证校准阈值检测漂移并进行选择性更新。实验结果表明，AdaptLSTM在保持高准确性的同时，显著提高了效率，并在不同数据集和模型骨干上表现出优越性。
AI.keywords: 云工作负载预测, 在线学习, 分布漂移, AdaptLSTM, 效率
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一种创新的自适应在线学习框架AdaptLSTM，有效地解决了云工作负载预测中常见的分布漂移问题。其核心创新在于结合了漂移检测和选择性更新机制，显著提高了学习效率和准确性。模型无关性是其另一个重要优势，使其能够广泛应用于不同的神经网络架构。这项工作对于需要在动态环境中进行实时预测的云服务和相关领域具有重要意义。

title: Telling FIBS: Probes Effectively Detect Sabotage and Catch Unverbalized Deception
comments: 11 pages main text, 118 pages total; 25 figures, 28 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/AlignmentResearch/fibs-probes
summary: Recent incidents have highlighted the challenge of monitoring LLM agents and the danger of models deceiving people. We show that white-box deception detection via probes can be scaled up to frontier monitoring settings by collecting the largest deception dataset to date for training probes and introducing a novel probe architecture which can aggregate information across many layers and tokens. Our probes surpass black-box monitors on agentic coding benchmarks, achieving 98.3% AUROC in SHADE-Arena and 98.0% in BashArena (vs. 97.7%, 97.6% resp. for action-only text monitors), and show improved efficacy as the underlying model is scaled up. We further test probes on several cases where deception cannot be determined from the context alone; in these cases of introspective deception, the ground truth can only be determined through careful elicitation or knowledge of a model's training data. In one such evaluation, we show that probes can distinguish transcripts containing a model's true hidden goal from other goals with an AUROC of up to 99.7%. Our probes also detect deception on prominent open-weight models which lie about politically sensitive topics when put under pressure. We release our training dataset, dubbed FIBS, to help drive frontier deployment of effective probes, and encourage the community to expand upon it with further examples of deception and sabotage.
